descriptions.github:5794107742: Two outcomes are recognised by name but have never been seen on a real parcel: a failed delivery and a parcel returned to the warehouse . They are mapped to problem and returning on the strength of GoBolt's own tracking page code, not on a parcel that actually went through them. Nothing at all is known about a parcel that is: - refused at the door, or undeliverable because of the address - held, delayed or rescheduled after a missed attempt - lost or damaged - cancelled before it ever shipped Today anything GoBolt reports that is not recognised falls back to the most recent step that is recognised, and logs a one-time warning with a ready-made issue link. That keeps the sensor sensible, but it means the parcel shows as still moving when it is really stuck. A parcel moves to the fast 15-minute refresh an hour before its expected…

descriptions.github:5793899293: Why Venus's rotation: is period h: -5832.5 (line 78 of registry/worlds.yaml ). NASA's Venus Fact Sheet ( read on , lists the sidereal rotation period as -5832.6 hours, one tenth of an hour different. Every other planet's period in this file has the same digits as its fact sheet; Venus is the exception, and no comment says where -5832.5 comes from. The difference is about two thousandths of one per cent of the period, far below anything the eye sees: this is about the number being traceable. Where registry/worlds.yaml , line 78: Nothing else in registry/ , scripts/ , site/js/ or tests/ mentions 5832. What to change Find where -5832.5 came from, and read the page or paper you use before you decide, because sources round a rotation period differently. descriptions.github:5793879813: Problem A watch of a video with English auto-captions failed with: The captions existed ( yt-dlp --list-subs shows en and en-orig auto-captions). Reproducing the caption leg by hand showed the actual cause: The operator is told the video has no captions, which points at the ASR path ( 6047) instead of "wait and retry". Cause plugins/knowledge/skills/video-digest/extraction/acquisition/acquire.js:332-343 : when the first caption selection fails in full mode, the captions-only retry runs; if that retry's spawn fails (here, a 429 that outlasted spawnWithAcquireRetry 's backoff budget in acquire-retry-policy.js ), its detail is dropped and the function returns the ladder message from selectCaptionFile instead. Fix When the caption retry's spawn fails, surface captionRetry.detail (classified retryable via isRetryableAcquireError ) rather than the ladder-exhausted message, so a rate limit…

descriptions.github:5791437029: Problem The supersession sweep ( ) already detects when a PR's claimed issue was closed by a different merged PR, but for human-authored PRs it only leaves a comment ("Leaving this contribution open…"). The PR then sits needs-rebase + CONFLICTING until a human notices. Example: 11411 ( ) fixed 11410; the hive's own 11413 merged the same one-line guard 16 minutes later. The sweep correctly identified the supersession at 11:54Z, but the PR stayed open until a maintainer closed it by hand. Proposal When the supersession sweep finds all of: 1. the PR's claimed issue(s) are closed, and the closing PR is a different, merged PR; 2. the PR is CONFLICTING against base (or every file it touches was also touched by the closing PR); 3. the diff is small (e.g. size/XS – size/M ) and no human has commented since the supersession notice for N hours (e.g. 24h); then close the PR with an explanatory…

descriptions.github:5791402196: Summary repowise impacted-tests --format json for a change to package.json gives different output on identical input from one process to the next. The run-all reasons come in a different order, and the namer a reason quotes changes ( scripts/name.py and 2 more in one run, tests/test pkg.py and 2 more or tests/helpers.py and 2 more in another). The cause is that the list of files naming a changed file is built in the iteration order of a frozenset , which Python's string hashing randomises per process. packages/core/src/repowise/core/analysis/test selection.py:362-365 ( file namers ): namers arrive in whatever order the caller iterates sources, and that order is never made stable. Mechanism - The sources come from the checkout's tracked files: git refs.tracked paths returns a frozenset ( core/git refs.py:89-91 ). The impacted-tests collection iterates it in hash order when building the…

descriptions.github:5791254909: On Windows, parliament doctor and parliament ask crash with UnicodeEncodeError when their output is redirected or piped, because stdout is then cp1252. Reproduce (Windows 11, Python 3.14, sys.stdout.encoding == "cp1252" when redirected): Both exit 1. ask raises the error once in the renderer and again in ask error , which tries to print the failure through the same console. parliament ask --json redirected works, because it doesn't print glyphs. Setting PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 fixes all of them. Why: cli.py uses a plain Console() when stdout is not a TTY. That console writes through the stream's own encoding, which on Windows is the ANSI code page when redirected. The TTY branch is fine in Windows Terminal. Who hits it: anyone running parliament doctor report.txt to attach to a bug report ( 14 asks for exactly that), CI logs on Windows, and anything that wraps the CLI without --json…

descriptions.github:5791078140: The import resume test should pass however the machine clock moves. Current state: TestApplyRunAgainFinishesAnImportAStopCutShort compares the site after a stopped and resumed import with the site after one uninterrupted run, in list order. Types list in the order they were created. Since 358 an imported type gets the real time, so the type an import adds lists last. The machine clock can step back between two writes, and WSL2 does this at times. That type then lists earlier in one of the two sites. The test fails, although both sites hold the same content. Proposal: compare the two sites with their types in key order, so only the content counts. Trigger: it failed this way twice in local runs while building 359.

descriptions.github:5790706543: PKZIP for z/OS supports IBM CPU-assisted compression and custom static dictionaries. PKWARE’s SecureZIP/PKZIP Server 12 MR5 can extract such archives without special hardware. The IBM i product added decompression of CMPSC-compressed z/OS files in release 10.0.5. Open questions the spec doesn’t settle: the byte order of the 4-byte length (the APPNOTE’s general rule is little-endian, but z/OS extra fields are big-endian); whether 0x40 means raw Deflate or zlib-wrapped; whether the length counts stored or inflated bytes; how the stream ends; the text says “CP instruction”, presumably a typo for CMPSC. Algorithm might be the same as Hercules cmpsc 2012.c which looks like a full unpack and pack implementation. See also

Users of the Xceed Zip Self-Extractor Module can use the BWT method by using the XCDSFXBZ.BIN binary. See and and Old versions at and but it is not yet investigated if this seeingly custom BWT method is implemented in them. Scope: propose deterministic additional checks in SYSTEM/preview gate.py, cast review.py or quality check.py, using sampled motion/rig/prop metrics rather than bypassing the existing image review. descriptions.github:5789067872: Long Blender production can stall. Matching completed clips can be reused, but automatic bounded recovery needs a focused design. Scope: inspect SYSTEM/cast renderer.py and host worker handling. Detect stalled progress, terminate the owned worker safely, and retry only matching verified work with a fixed retry budget. Acceptance: synthetic/mocked stall, worker failure and successful resume cases; no unbounded restart loop; input bytes and prior verified delivery preserved; no unrelated processes terminated. Keep failure evidence and report actual retry counts.
descriptions.github:5789067517: The current stylized cast is functional but acting and hand/prop contact need more expressive, reusable behavior. Scope: improve registered expressions or interactions in SYSTEM/cast renderer.py and character modules. Start with one bounded action such as a questioning glance or a coin handoff; discuss the action contract before expanding it. Acceptance: demonstrate multiple synthetic characters with stable identities, actual motion, correct prop ownership and no intersecting/broken limbs. Include reproducible preview settings and existing test results. Avoid a one-story hardcoded animation.
descriptions.github:5789067182: Current automatic cast routing depends on registered English role words. Hindi narratives should be able to select source-supported multi-character direction without requiring English role names. Scope: inspect SYSTEM/cast contract.py and the cast-routing code. Propose a bounded multilingual role vocabulary/normalization layer rather than inventing actors from unrelated text. Acceptance: positive Hindi/English and mixed-script synthetic cases; negative nonhuman/single-person cases; identity consistency and exact cue ordering preserved. Unsupported roles must stay explicit. Update documentation and meaningful contract tests.

descriptions.github:5788818399: Motivation Time-series datasets frequently suffer from data leakage during naive rolling aggregations. We need an automated agent recipe that detects temporal ordering columns and safely computes rolling statistics (mean, volatility, EWMA) and lag windows using Polars rolling and shift operations. Proposed Heuristics 1. Check for temporal or monotonically increasing index columns. 2. Formulate rolling windows without forward-looking bias. 3. Quantify autocorrelations and propose predictive lag offsets. PRs and suggestions welcome!

descriptions.github:5788657537: Real-model chemistry accuracy has not been measured. We need an evaluation that separates image/structure reading from reaction feasibility and avoids only testing successful textbook reactions. Propose a small openly licensed/synthetic set with positive, negative, missing-condition and ambiguous-structure cases across chemistry domains. Specify conditions, justified labels, uncertainty scoring and how to report each error type. How to see it Update a product by SKU, then look for an audit entry for it; compare with the same change made on the product's admin screen. descriptions.github:5788326101: Repositories that use detect-secrets mark known non-secrets with an inline pragma: allowlist secret comment, for example: Repowise still reports these lines, and they can surface as "rotate this hard-coded secret" in repowise next . descriptions.github:5788325652: After a repository folder is moved or copied (with its .repowise/ ), repowise next reports "unavailable" and repowise health --refactoring-targets says "No stored refactoring analysis". The MCP tools keep working. Cause: repo index session in packages/cli/src/repowise/cli/helpers.py (around line 287) looks the repository up by exact local path ( get repository by path ), which still holds the old location. Suggested fix: when the path lookup misses and the repo-local store holds exactly one repository row, use that row (optionally with a hint that repowise update re-registers the path). descriptions.github:5786309473: Today real-time protection reacts when a file is written. On Linux, fanotify permission events ( FAN OPEN EXEC PERM / FAN OPEN PERM ) let a privileged daemon allow or deny each open/exec before it happens. Scope - Optional root-only service ( sentinel-vision-cli daemon --on-access ) using fanotify via ctypes - Scan on FAN OPEN EXEC PERM , deny if a signature engine matches, with a short timeout that defaults to allow - Cache verdicts by (dev, inode, mtime) and exclude the daemon's own I/O - systemd unit + docs Notes Needs CAP SYS ADMIN ; must never deadlock the system (fail-open on timeouts). Part of the roadmap. --- Generated by Claude Code

descriptions.github:5785981137: What Two places resolve an untrusted path and then read from it, with no check that the result stays in the intended tree. 1. the quoted form of use in a unit — tools/lomentc.py: : The quoted form of use is stored raw by the parser. An absolute path is taken as-is; a relative one is joined onto root / cur base and .resolve() d — and the normalized result is never compared for containment. A library containing use "../../../../etc/passwd" (or an absolute path) makes the compiler read and parse a file outside the project. A FIFO or device path reaches read text and wedges the build. 2. pkg.json path — tools/lompkg.py:65-68 : rel is only checked to be a str ; pkg hash ( tools/lompkg.py:26 ) then rglob s that resolved directory and SHA-256s every .lomt under it. {"path": "../../../../"} makes it walk and hash an arbitrary ancestor. descriptions.github:5785976623: What The native heap's free is tools/lomentc.py:229 define internal void (ptr %p) . It computes the block offset straight from the pointer with no validation: There is no check that %p lies in [ , + ) or that it was ever allocated. sub i32 / trunc wrap, and the GEP into the fixed [65536 x i8] heap is unguarded. free is an ordinary builtin — a program can hand it a foreign pointer via the boundary builtins, e.g. free(ptr add(p, 100)) , producing an out-of-bounds read (and, on the link path, an out-of-bounds store into a fixed global). The block header carries only a size (at +0 ) and a next (at +4 ) — no free bit . So a second free is indistinguishable from a first: - 1st free of a tail block: %istail is true → rewind → store i32 %hi, ptr (the frontier rolls back). - 2nd free of the same %p : %hend != %off now, so it falls into link and inserts hi into the free list. The region [hi…
descriptions.github:5785976363: What lompi 's identity is a content hash over the package's sources. The reader it uses is capped by construction, so the "too big" check that is supposed to protect the hash can never fire. lompi/lpi sys.lomt:126-136 — the read loop's bound is cap , so sys read file can never return more than cap : Given that, this guard is dead — lompi/lpi pkg.lomt:613-616 : got PKG FILE MAX is unreachable ( PKG FILE MAX = 262144 , lpi pkg.lomt:504 ). A 300 KiB file reads as exactly 262144 , neither arm fires, and the hash is computed over the truncated content. The same dead check is repeated in pkg check ( lpi pkg.lomt:900 ) and in the install copy ( lpi cli.lomt:983 ). Why it matters The function's own docstring states the opposite intent — lpi pkg.lomt:596 : 有文件读不出来或超过 PKG FILE MAX 时返回 0 . So: - Pinning breaks. Build a library whose lib.lomt is a valid 256 KiB prefix plus a tail, pin it in…

descriptions.github:5785930227: What SECURITY.md property 1 requires that an index outside [lo..hi] "traps, with no other side effect." The IR backend gets this right: the audit increment lives only in the pass block gok , and the trap block is a bare call void () / unreachable (runtime llvm.trap() ). The Rust backend does it in the wrong order — tools/lomentc.py:310-317 : and the guard is lowered as an unconditional call ( tools/lomentc.py: ): Why it matters On the Rust target (the --emit-rust / no std / kernel path) a violating index writes LOMENT AUDIT[cap] before trapping. If the panic is caught/unwound, the audit count now exceeds the number of guards that passed — property 2 — and the trap is no longer side-effect-free — property 1. Reproduced with 17 capabilities and a guard on the 17th: followed by store i64 — an out-of-bounds write to a fixed global whenever that guard passes. descriptions.github:5785929269: What lomt from.py turns a Potato form object into a .lomt interface unit, and that unit is fed straight to the frozen core ( lomt from.py:9 : ... --lomt from-- .lomt (进入冻结核心) ). Every artifact-controlled string that reaches the emitted source must be a literal , not an interpolation. excluded is the one that is not — tools/lomt from.py:408-412 : The only upstream validation is "non-empty string" — tools/potato.py:641-645 : A " or a newline is not rejected. An artifact whose excluded entry contains a quote and a newline closes the literal early and starts a new top-level declaration , which the core then compiles: emits which is valid Loment. The injected declaration can carry a full body, so this is artifact → compiled code. Why it matters The stated contract of this tool is that Potato is a representation layer — it records "what exists", not "how it is computed" ( lomt from.py:13 )…

descriptions.github:5785903469: openclaw/README.md (lines 66 and 73), docs/guide/getting-started/supported-agents.md (line 192), src/hooks/README.md and the ApprovalOwner doc in src/hooks/decision.rs say that with RTK REWRITE HOST=openclaw , RTK stops asking only for commands that matched no rule. ApprovalOwner::apply relaxes every PermissionVerdict::Default , and a chain whose commands are only partly covered by allow rules is also Default . With only Bash(cargo test) allowed: An explicit ask rule still gives 3 and a deny still gives 2 under openclaw, so this is a docs mismatch, not a gate bypass: OpenClaw applies its own approval to the rewrite. 4204 describes it in rtk rewrite --help as "turns every 3 but an ask rule's into 0". descriptions.github:5785902607: As a patient, I want the app to notice when I go quiet while looking at a memory and gently play a loved one's recording, so that I'm encouraged to keep remembering and talking. Behavior While a photo is open, the microphone measures audio levels to tell speech from silence. It does not record or transcribe. When silence exceeds a threshold (default 5 seconds, configurable), the app plays the relative's recording attached to that photo. Playback does not restart if the patient resumes speaking. For each photo and session, the app stores speech duration and pause count. These are the only values saved.

An attacker who encodes a payload any other way currently gets through the evasion check, even though the visible text scores below the threshold. Encodings not covered today, all trivially reversible: - hex ( 69676e6f72652070726576696f7573 ) - ROT13 - reversed text - base32 - UTF-16 / UTF-7 smuggling - HTML entities ( ig... ) What to do 1. Add the candidates to decode candidates() . It is a generator, so adding cheap attempts costs nothing when there is nothing to decode. 2. Reject decodes that are not mostly printable, as the base64 branch already does. 3. Add a fixture and a test in tests/test semantic.py for each encoding you add, asserting the "Encoded payload inside description" finding fires. 4. Add a benign test: a description containing a hex-looking value (a SHA-256 digest, say)…

descriptions.github:5784433916: Peak RSS on the benchmark device is 350.7 MB against a 400 MB ceiling. descriptions.github:5784431975: RATL-Bench-v0 is 150 clips, 5 reciters, 30 ayat, 1,374 words. That is a Week-1 feasibility probe doing duty as a release gate, and it is the single biggest caveat on every published number. The held-out G3/G4 tier is 400 non-bench ayat from two reciters — the only two the frozen model never trained on. Useful contributions: more reciters with word-level timings (CC BY 4.0 or compatible); more speed and style variety; a larger reciter-disjoint held-out set. Everything is generated from manifests, so a contribution is a manifest plus a licence, not a pile of audio. Read first: spike/corpus/ratl-bench-v0.json , eval/corpus/mutate.py . Reciter-disjoint splits are mandatory (SPEC §3.2).
descriptions.github:5784431482: V1 never emits SUBSTITUTION ; suspected substitutions surface as UNCERTAIN (SPEC §4.1). Measured: of 10,560 threshold configurations on the selection tier, 768 met the false-reject budget and coverage floor, and none retained substitution detection . The cheapest substitution-active configuration cost a held-out FRR near 0.08 against a 0.05 ceiling. The signal that failed was a per-word acoustic gap, mean(max logp) − mean(logp at path label) . Reciter-normalising it (leave-one-out robust z-score within the clip) lifted held-out precision from 0.0368 to 0.2093 — a real improvement, still nowhere near enough. What would move this: a signal that distinguishes "a different word was said here" from "this reciter's voice fits the model poorly" . The second currently dominates. Definition of done: substitution precision high enough that enabling it keeps held-out G4 ≤ 0.05, demonstrated on a…
descriptions.github:5784430982: Boundary accuracy degrades monotonically with word duration, measured across every reciter: | Ground-truth duration | n | accuracy | |---|---|---| | 0–500 ms | 109 | 0.9495 | | 500–1000 ms | 427 | 0.8923 | | 1000–2000 ms | 556 | 0.8399 | | 2000–4000 ms | 229 | 0.7686 | | 4000 ms | 53 | 0.4906 | The ±150 ms tolerance is fixed, so a 4 s madd demands 3.75% relative precision while a 500 ms word needs 30%. This is also why slow mujawwad scores 0.7230 — it is the style with the longest words, not a distinct failure mode. Known unexploited lead: during Exp 2, decode variant V win 25 (boundary-posterior DP constrained to ±0.5 s) scored 0.8264 on Mujawwad versus 0.7934 for the shipped decoder, while losing overall. A duration-conditional hybrid was declined at the time because it added a selection degree of freedom for 0.01 overall. With a larger corpus it may be worth revisiting. Read first…
descriptions.github:5784430457: V1 ships a Kotlin/JVM core (SPEC §6.1). Rust + UniFFI was deferred deliberately, with the cost stated openly: a JVM core makes the Python and JS/WASM bindings materially harder, and deferred ports have a habit of never happening. This issue is the counterweight. ratl-core is a bounded body of numeric code — feature windowing, a Viterbi lattice, a boundary rule, a taxonomy — with no Android or platform dependencies . It has an executable specification: the conformance vectors in conformance/vectors/ (T0–T3) pin every function from pure arithmetic up to a full Assessment . Definition of done: a Rust ratl-core passing all four conformance tiers, and ratl-eval reproducing G2 = 0.8570 on RATL-Bench-v0 from the Rust path. Start here: ratl-core/src/main/kotlin/ai/ratl/core/ForcedAligner.kt and ErrorLattice.kt . Read the comments about tie-breaking before you begin — they are correctness, not…

descriptions.github:5784117328: The core claim of this project is falsifiability : the verifier ( prototype/verify certificate.py ) re-derives every decision independently, and prototype/test adversarial certificates.py holds the current kill count (200 forgeries, 0 accepted). Challenge: construct a certificate the verifier accepts that the engine never issued — tamper with fields, recompute CERT HASH, swap INPUT HASH, anything. Rules: 1. Report what you tried in a comment on this issue (what broke, which check caught it). 2. If you succeed, open an issue titled forgery accepted with the artifact — that is a real bug and will be treated as a priority fix, with credit in the CHANGELOG. 3. No access to secrets is needed: everything is local and pure Python. This is the project's way of saying: don't trust us, attack us.

descriptions.github:5783653594: Summary Store.GC skips directories when it walks blobs/ , but not when it walks blobs/ / . A directory under blobs/ / whose name happens to be a valid encoded digest is treated as a blob, so if it is unreachable it reaches os.Remove — which fails on a non-empty directory and aborts the whole GC. Noticed while scoping 1521 (the OCI-layout blob sweep, which has to decide what to do with the same entries). Not caused by that work; filing separately so it is not bundled into a feature issue. Where content/oci/oci.go , in the collection loop of GC : blobDigest.Validate() only checks that the name is a well-formed digest for the algorithm; it says nothing about the entry being a regular file. So the inner loop has no equivalent of the outer IsDir() guard. - main (v3): lines 591-622 - v2 : lines 492-520 — identical code Reproduction In an OCI layout, create an unreachable directory whose name…

descriptions.github:5783499055: Today the desk checks tools and budget when the report arrives. The stronger guarantee is to enforce them while the worker works . descriptions.github:5783321287: Teams of Dots: a Researcher hands a brief to a Writer, and the result comes back to the Researcher's conversation. Proposal - Grants: the owner allows "can hand work to" between specific Dots. - Tool: a delegate to dot tool starts a turn in a new conversation of the target Dot and returns at once. When that turn finishes, its final message is posted back to the original conversation. - Limits: a maximum depth of 2, no cycles, and at most 3 hand-offs per turn. - Isolation: the target Dot keeps its own model, permissions, approvals and computer. Please comment with a design before starting.
descriptions.github:5783320610: Let external services start work: for example, a new GitHub issue asks the Triage Dot to label it. Proposal - Each trigger has its own URL ( POST /api/hooks/:id ) and a secret that is shown once when created. - Auth modes: bearer token, or an HMAC-SHA256 signature (for example GitHub's X-Hub-Signature-256 ). - Use a constant-time comparison, a body size limit and rate limiting. Secrets never appear in logs or API responses. - Each event becomes a turn in the trigger's conversation. The payload is passed as clearly marked, size-limited, untrusted data. - Triggers obey pauses, approvals and the one-turn-per-Dot lock. This is a larger feature. Please comment with a short design before starting.
descriptions.github:5783320337: Owners cannot see how many tokens each Dot uses. Proposal - Record input and output tokens, call counts and cost per Dot per day. Take the provider's usage fields when it reports them; OpenRouter reports cost. - Show today's and this month's usage in the Dot form, and a total in Settings. - Add an optional daily warning threshold that sends a notification through the existing NOTIFY WEBHOOK URL . Please discuss the data model in the issue before opening a pull request.

descriptions.github:5781149669: Gemma, Qwen and Flash Next continue a conversation from saved model state, so a follow-up only processes the new tokens. GPT-OSS doesn't: every follow-up and every tool result reprocesses the whole conversation. In the first community benchmark (16 GB M2), the follow-up on GPT-OSS 20B reused 0 of 1,400 tokens and took 22 s to start, where Qwen3.6 reused 1,407 tokens and started in 2.8 s. On GPT-OSS 120B, where a short prompt already takes about a minute, that makes agent loops very slow. descriptions.github:5781148758: Nobody has gone through TUFF with VoiceOver yet. Some views have accessibility labels, but there has been no end-to-end check. What would help most Turn on VoiceOver (⌘F5) and try to: 1. install a model from the Models screen; 2. start a chat, send a message, and hear the answer; 3. turn on Web search with the globe button and open a citation from the answer; 4. run a quick benchmark on the Benchmarks screen; 5. change a setting. Write down where VoiceOver is silent, reads something unhelpful (like an icon name), or where you cannot reach a control. The audit on its own is a valuable contribution, even if you do not fix anything. Post your findings here, and if you want to fix some of them, small pull requests that each address one screen are easiest to review. Views live in Sources/TUFFApp/Mac .
descriptions.github:5781148393: TUFF already has ⌘1 to ⌘5 for the main screens, ⌘N for a new chat, ⌘↩ to send and ⌘. to stop. What's missing is moving between conversations and getting back to the message box without the mouse. Proposal - Previous and next conversation, for example ⌘[ and ⌘], or ⌃Tab and ⌃⇧Tab, whichever fits macOS conventions best. - A shortcut to put focus back in the message box. Put them in the Navigate menu (see Sources/TUFFApp/Mac/App/AppNavigationCommands.swift ) so they're discoverable, and check they don't clash with text-editing shortcuts. Search for keyboardShortcut in Sources/TUFFApp to see the existing ones. How to check Build with swift build -c release , run .build/release/TUFF , and include a screenshot of the menu. A note on how you tested it is enough. Gemma 4 E2B is plenty for testing. Comment with your shortcut choices before building so we can agree on them.

descriptions.github:5781147689: Every TUFF release is tested on one machine: a 16 GB M2 MacBook Air. The memory floors in the model table and the Auto settings were all chosen from that one Mac. We don't know how TUFF does on 8 GB Macs, Pro and Max chips, or M3 to M5. TUFF 8.1 has a built-in benchmark, so this takes a few clicks: 1. Update to TUFF 8.1.0 or newer. 2. Open Benchmarks , tick a model or two, and press Run Benchmark . 3. Press Share on GitHub and post it. Or from the terminal: tuff bench --models gemma4 --share . Your result shows up on the leaderboard. Especially wanted: - any 8 GB Mac with Gemma 4 E2B, E4B or 26B-A4B; - a Mac with 32 GB or more running GPT-OSS 120B or Qwen3.8 Flash Next; - M4 and M5 machines. No need to comment here; the post is enough. Comment if something went wrong.

descriptions.github:5781146752: MetricFormat.memory( :) in Sources/TUFFApp/MacPresentation/MetricFormat.swift converts a UInt64 with Int64(bytes) . A value above Int64.max crashes the app. The storage( :) function right below it already uses Int64(clamping:) . Real memory figures will not reach that size, but a corrupted diagnostic or an uninitialised sentinel could, and a display formatter should never crash the app. What to change Use Int64(clamping: bytes) and add a test (a new MetricFormatTests.swift under Tests/TUFFApp/MacPresentation/ is fine) that formats UInt64.max without trapping. How to check Scripts/test.sh --filter MetricFormat . No model is needed. This is a one-line fix plus a test, which makes it a good way to learn the pull request process.
descriptions.github:5781146333: TUFFCLI --help says: But --top-k 0 on its own is rejected, because --top-p defaults to 0.95 and top-p needs top-k between 1 and 256 when sampling. That rule is deliberate and tested in Tests/TUFFEngine/Core/CLI/CLIArgumentsTests.swift ; only the help text is misleading. What to change - The help line in Sources/TUFFCLI/Args.swift (around line 153), so it says what actually works, for example 0 = off with --top-p 1 . - Optionally, the error message near line 440, so someone who passes --top-k 0 is told to add --top-p 1 . How to check Scripts/test.sh --filter CLIArguments . Add a small assertion that the usage text mentions --top-p 1 . No model is needed.

descriptions.github:5781062427: Goal: publish schemas/e3bundle-report.schema.json (draft 2020-12) describing the JSON printed by e3bundle verify , so CI users can validate it. Fields today: format , bundle id , manifest hash , status (VERIFIED|FAILED|ERROR), files declared , files verified , signatures present , signatures valid , signatures trusted (int or null), trust mode , min signatures , findings , limitations . ERROR reports contain only status , findings , limitations . Files: schemas/e3bundle-report.schema.json , a test that validates the reports of both example bundles against it, README link. Acceptance: schema matches current output exactly (no field renames — that would be a breaking change); test passes on Linux CI. Adding jsonschema as a test-only dependency is fine if justified. Reviewer:
descriptions.github:5781062038: Goal: a README.es.md with the product part of the README (from the title down to Roadmap ) translated into Spanish, and a language link at the top of both files. Files: README.es.md (new), one link line in README.md . Acceptance: commands, flags, exit codes and JSON keys stay in English and unchanged; the six Limits bullets keep their meaning exactly; no new claims. The E3-001 protocol section can link to the English README instead of being translated. Checks: python scripts/validate public snapshot.py --root . passes; every relative link resolves. Reviewer:
descriptions.github:5781061694: Goal: cover two corruption cases that are not tested yet. 1. signatures.json is truncated or not valid JSON → verify must report a finding and exit 1 (not crash). 2. manifest.json contains bytes that are not valid UTF-8 → verify must exit 2 with status: ERROR . Files: tests/test e3bundle.py (fixtures created in a temporary directory, synthetic data only). Acceptance: both tests pass on Linux CI; if a case crashes, fix scripts/e3bundle.py in the same PR. Tests to run: python -m pytest tests/test e3bundle.py -v Reviewer:
descriptions.github:5781061339: Goal: when e3bundle exits with code 2, the message should say what went wrong and how to fix it. Cases: bundle directory does not exist; manifest.json missing (suggest e3bundle manifest ); --trusted-keys file missing or not a JSON object; private key file unreadable in sign . Files: scripts/e3bundle.py , tests/test e3bundle.py . Acceptance: each case prints one actionable sentence (no Python traceback), exit codes unchanged (0/1/2), JSON output for verify keeps status: ERROR . Tests to run: python -m pytest tests -v — add one test per case. Reviewer:

descriptions.github:5780811691: For everyone When an admin opens the edit window for a Region (and the same window is used for Areas, Territories, Sectors and AOs) in the Admin app, the browser's developer console prints a warning: "A component is changing an uncontrolled input to be controlled." Nothing visibly breaks, and saving still works, but in development the warning also shows up as a red "1 Issue" badge in the corner of the screen, which hides real problems and confuses people who are debugging. It happens because the read-only "ID" box in that window starts out empty-and-unset while the organization's details are still loading, then gets a value once they arrive. The fix is a one-line change that gives the box an empty value until the ID is known. Found while testing a different change locally, and it also happens on main . A console.log that nobody routes goes to stdout with no request context (see the logging-facade issue), and an async callback inside setTimeout whose promise rejects is silent by default in Node. The general lesson: the lint config does not…
descriptions.github:5780756531: Problem Clients — SDKs, dashboards, monitoring agents, and the operator UIs the README describes — can only act on information they can reliably find in responses. Several such headers are missing, inconsistent, or undocumented: - src/config/cors.config.ts exposes only one: exposedHeaders: ["X-Total-Count"] . So X-RateLimit- and Retry-After are not exposed to browser clients even if the server sets them — meaning a dashboard in a browser cannot implement throttling. - allowedHeaders is ["Content-Type", "Authorization", "X-Requested-With"] , so a client cannot even send an X-Request-Id for correlation. - There is no X-Request-Id on responses at all, so a user reporting a problem cannot quote an id that maps to server logs. - x-powered-by is disabled (good), but the CORS X-Requested-With allowance is not obviously serving a purpose. Why it matters This is the API equivalent of a page with…
descriptions.github:5780756364: Problem src/health/health.service.ts returns HealthResponseDto from three endpoints — /health/live (line 25), /health/ready (42), /health/startup (70) — with status , timestamp , uptime , and a components map of ComponentStatusDto . The implementation is careful: it checks the database and Redis in parallel ( Promise.all , lines 36-39), honours HEALTH CHECK TIMEOUT MS (22-24), and treats Redis as () . The gap is the vocabulary. What values can status take? Is it a string, or an enum? Is the whole components map guaranteed present, or per-probe? Is a failing component distinguishable from an absent one? A monitoring integration cannot reliably branch on any of that, so in practice operators read the raw JSON to work out whether the service is degraded or down. docs/kubernetes-health-probes.md exists and presumably documents the probe contract — check it against the DTO, since drift here…
descriptions.github:5780756184: Problem The repository publishes generated TypeScript and Python SDKs from docs/openapi.json , built by /openapi-generator-cli (CI generates typescript-fetch and python clients). Generated method names come from each operation's operationId . Without an explicit operationId , the generator derives one from the HTTP method and path — so GET /portfolio/portfolios and GET /portfolio/:portfolioId/performance produce names like portfolioPortfoliosGet . The README already shows exactly this style: That name is derived, not declared. It encodes the current path, so it is unstable under refactoring: rename a route, nest a controller, or move an endpoint under /api/v1 , and every consumer's method name changes in the next SDK release. Why it matters Generated SDK method names are the primary API surface for consumers, and they are derived from an implementation detail (the URL path). An…
descriptions.github:5780755936: Problem The OpenAPI spec is generated from decorators, and the decorators are incomplete. A count across the 41 controllers found 377 route decorators ( / / / / ) but only 209 decorators — so roughly 168 operations have no documented responses, and many have no summary either. This directly harms generated SDKs: swagger-ui-express and the OpenAPI generator both use these strings, so an operation with no summary surfaces in the SDK and in Swagger UI as an unnamed method. The README advertises both generated SDKs as the primary integration surface. The good news is that the framework for this already exists and is used consistently in places — , , , , are all in use, and file-upload.controller.ts is a well-documented example. Two concrete gaps: 1. message is polymorphic. src/common/pipes/validation.pipe.ts:58-63 returns message as an array of strings, while a plain throw new BadRequestException("Payload has expired") ( src/blockchain/oracle/services/submitter.service.ts:229 ) produces a string . descriptions.github:5780755605: Problem src/config/helmet.config.ts defines a Content Security Policy that is simultaneously too permissive and potentially broken: 'unsafe-inline' in scriptSrc substantially defeats the purpose of a CSP for XSS: it permits inline script execution, which is what most XSS payloads need. The cdn.jsdelivr.net allowance exists so Swagger UI can load its assets, and swagger-ui-express is a dependency. imgSrc includes " which is an odd allowance for a policy applied to all responses. HSTS is configured correctly ( maxAge: 31536000, includeSubDomains: true, preload: true ). Why it matters A CSP with 'unsafe-inline' in scriptSrc is close to no protection against script injection. If an injection point exists anywhere in the API's responses, this policy will not stop it. Meanwhile SanitizePipe handles XSS in request bodies, which is a different thing — response-context injection is not covered…
descriptions.github:5780755400: Problem There is no secret scanning in .github/workflows/build-check.yml , which runs only: install → codegen diff → tsc --noEmit → a narrow Jest subset → build, plus an OpenAPI/SDK job on pushes. Meanwhile the repository is unusually exposed to credential leaks: - .env.example , .env.production.example , .env.secrets.template are all committed (correctly, as templates) - npm run security:generate-secrets runs a shell script ( scripts/generate-secrets.sh ) that creates secrets - security:check ( package.json:28 ) runs npm audit , lint, and the KYC guard scan — but no secret scan , and it is not wired into CI - The README (line 107) warns "Never commit .env files" Nothing enforces that warning. Why it matters A committed secret is permanent in git history even after a later commit removes it, and anyone cloning gets it. On a project handling wallet signing keys, JWT secrets, and provider…

descriptions.github:5780754736: Problem src/infrastructure/webhooks/ lets a subscriber register an endpoint that the API will later POST to. The module has five services, none tested: - webhook-subscription.service.ts — presumably stores the target URL - webhook-delivery.service.ts — performs the outbound request - webhook-processor.service.ts , webhook-event.service.ts , webhook-hmac.service.ts And the controller that accepts registrations ( webhook.controller.ts ) hardcodes const userId = "system" at eight sites — lines 53, 65, 76, 89, 100, 110, 127, and 196 — meaning subscription ownership is not enforced either. If the stored URL is not validated, an authenticated user can register an endpoint pointing at internal infrastructure and the API will dutifully request it, with retries and error logging that confirm reachability. This interacts with an open question in this backlog: GET /auth/logout is documented in the README (line 197) as "client-side token removal", which suggests a stateless token model with no server-side session cookie. descriptions.github:5780632286: Why this helps The store takes automatic pre-migration SQLite backups, but there is no explicit command to preserve a complete current store. A .vwx transfer archive intentionally exports selected reporting inputs and is not a full database backup. Copying only the live .db file is unsafe when committed data remains in WAL. Deprecated APIs and parameters in use: android.view.Window.setStatusBarColor android.view.Window.setNavigationBarColor LAYOUT IN DISPLAY CUTOUT MODE SHORT EDGES Why this matters On Android 15 and higher, apps targeting SDK 35 are edge to edge by default, and the status bar and navigation bar color APIs no longer have an effect. Continuing to use them can lead to incorrect visuals (content behind system bars, wrong contrast) and Google Play may flag the app in the pre-launch checks. Acceptance criteria [ ] Play Console no longer lists the deprecated APIs after the next release [ ] Reader, library and settings screens render correctly under the status bar and navigation bar [ ] Content is not hidden behind display cutouts or gesture…

descriptions.github:5775416270: What The repo has a .prettierrc , but there's no script to run Prettier and several files are not formatted with it (e.g. server/src/app.ts , server/src/server.ts , server/src/utils/env.ts , server/src/utils/logger.ts , server/src/middleware/ .ts , server/src/docs/openapi.ts ). As a result, contributors' editors reformat unrelated lines and PR diffs get noisy. Suggested approach - Add "format": "prettier --write ." and "format:check": "prettier --check ." to the root package.json (Prettier is already a root devDependency) - Add a .prettierignore ( dist , node modules , pnpm-lock.yaml , coverage , …) - Run pnpm format once in a separate, formatting-only commit - Mention pnpm format in CONTRIBUTING.md Acceptance criteria - [ ] pnpm format:check passes on main - [ ] The formatting commit contains no logic changes
descriptions.github:5775414877: What Express logs a deprecation warning whenever the refresh-token cookie is cleared: Every res.clearCookie('refreshToken', cookieOptions) call (in authController.ts , refreshTokenController.ts and userController.ts ) passes the shared cookieOptions from server/src/utils/constants.ts , and those options include maxAge . Suggested approach - In constants.ts , export a clearCookieOptions that is the same as cookieOptions without maxAge (keep httpOnly , sameSite: 'none' and secure , because the browser only clears a cookie when these attributes match) - Use it in every res.clearCookie(...) call Acceptance criteria - [ ] pnpm -F /server test no longer prints the deprecation warning - [ ] Logout and refresh still clear the cookie in the browser
descriptions.github:5775414106: What POST /api/v1/forms returns a 500 instead of a 400 when the request body has no elements array. In createForm ( server/src/controllers/formController.ts ) the code does elements.length === 0 before checking that elements exists, so a body like { "name": "My form" } throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined and ends up as a generic "Something went wrong!" error. Suggested approach - Add a createFormSchema (zod) to packages/validation/src/index.ts : name is a non-empty string and elements is a non-empty array. The other controllers already validate this way, e.g. registerSchema in authController.ts . - Use safeParseAsync in createForm and return new AppError('Validation failed!', 400, fieldErrors) like the other controllers do. - Remember to rebuild the shared package: pnpm -F /validation build . Acceptance criteria - [ ] A missing or empty elements or name returns 400…
descriptions.github:5775413392: What Deleting a form leaves its responses behind. deleteForm and deleteForms in server/src/controllers/formController.ts remove the Form documents, but the matching FormResponse documents ( server/src/models/formResponseModel.ts , field form ) stay in the database forever. Suggested approach - In deleteForm , after the form is deleted, also run FormResponse.deleteMany({ form: req.params.id }) - In deleteForms (bulk delete), run FormResponse.deleteMany({ form: { $in: forms } }) - (Alternative: a Mongoose findOneAndDelete / deleteMany middleware on the form schema) Acceptance criteria - [ ] Deleting one form or bulk-deleting forms also removes their responses - [ ] A test in server/src/test/ covers it (see auth.test.ts for the Supertest + in-memory MongoDB setup)
descriptions.github:5775413011: BENCHMARKS.md records that corerec.engines.SASRec "did not finish one epoch in 28 min" on ML-1M. In fit() , negatives are drawn one at a time inside for in range(self.neg samples) and a per-user loop, with a Python membership check for each draw. Fix: draw all negatives for a batch with one rng.integers(...) call and resample only the collisions, vectorised. Keep the cap that stops a user who has seen every item from hanging fit() ( test user who saw every item does not hang fit ). Measure: time one epoch on ML-1M before and after, and put the numbers in the PR. Recommendations on a fixed seed should keep similar quality: tests/test scale.py::test sasrec predicts from the newest position must still pass.
descriptions.github:5775412622: What The repo has no CI, so nothing checks PRs automatically. Add a GitHub Actions workflow that runs the same checks contributors are asked to run locally (see CONTRIBUTING.md). Suggested approach Create .github/workflows/ci.yml that runs on push to main and on pull request : 1. actions/checkout , pnpm/action-setup (version comes from packageManager in the root package.json ), actions/setup-node with Node 22 and cache: pnpm 2. pnpm install --frozen-lockfile 3. pnpm -F /validation build 4. pnpm -F /server exec tsc --noEmit and pnpm -F /server test (the tests use mongodb-memory-server , so no database secret is needed) 5. pnpm -F /client lint , pnpm -F /client test , pnpm -F /client build Acceptance criteria - [ ] The workflow passes on main - [ ] It runs for pull requests from forks (no secrets required) - [ ] Optional: add a CI status badge to the README

descriptions.github:5775341347: Where: faircode/cli.py ( --encoding ), faircode/loaders extra.py , faircode/mcp server.py . Current gap: --encoding ( 843) applies to delimited text, JSON and stdin. For .xlsx and .parquet input it is accepted and silently ignored, so a user who passes it for a workbook gets no sign that nothing happened, and the MCP encoding parameter behaves the same. Repro: (no warning that the flag was not used) Suggested approach: print a one-line stderr notice ("--encoding has no effect on .xlsx/.parquet files") from the CLI, and return a notes entry from the MCP tools, the way ignored-sheet notes already work. descriptions.github:5775340985: Where: faircode/proxy.py split held out spec() , assets/profiler-heldout.js , SPEC section 3. Current gap: 822 made --proxy-hints-with PATH=COLUMN:KEY split the text after = on its last colon. A held-out column whose own name contains a colon ( a:b , race:self reported , common in exports from survey tools) used to work as PATH=a:b ; it is now read as column a joined on key b , and fails with a misleading "column 'a' not found". Existing scripts that name such a column break with no hint why. Repro: Suggested approach: only treat the suffix as a key when it names a real column of the profiled dataset, or let a backslash escape a literal colon ( PATH=a\:b ); when the text after the colon is not a column, fall back to the whole string as the column name. Document the rule in SPEC section 3 and test both forms in tests/test proxy.py .
descriptions.github:5775340635: Where: faircode/compare.py , faircode/report.py compare to terminal() / compare to html() / compare to csv() , assets/profiler-compare.js . Current gap: compare builds drift flags from the two profiles' numbers but drops each profile's own data-quality flags. Two datasets with implausible ages ( 840) or with no column recognised by name ( 847) compare cleanly, with nothing in the drift report saying one side's age dimension lost values to the --max-age rule, so a drift in the 75+ share can be an artefact nobody is told about. Repro: Suggested approach: carry implausible values per side onto each shared dimension in the compare result (optional key, present only when above zero) and add a drift flag when it differs between A and B; mirror in the JS compare and cover it in the cross-engine compare parity test.
descriptions.github:5775340220: Where: faircode/cli.py ( write csv export , the profile / compare argument parsers). Current gap: PR 850 ("Add --csv-bom option for Excel compatibility", addressing 846) only added a bom=False parameter to write csv export() . No --csv-bom argument was ever added to the parsers and no caller passes bom , so the code path is dead and 846 (Excel on Windows garbling non-ASCII labels in --csv exports) is not actually fixed, even though it was closed. Repro: Suggested approach: add --csv-bom to both profile and compare , pass bom=args.csv bom at the two write csv export call sites (it needs --csv , like --csv-provenance ), document it in the README and SPEC.md section 12, and test that the file starts with \xef\xbb\xbf and that stdout output starts with U+FEFF.

Those are almost always sentinel codes for "unknown" - exactly the data-quality fact the new flag exists to surface - and they are indistinguishable from genuinely blank cells in the report. That is honest but unhelpful: the column carries exactly the information needed to audit age representation, and detection already recognises yob and birth as age columns. Current gap: 810 now marks a hint low expected when more than 20% of contingency cells expect fewer than 5 rows, but the p-value is still the chi-squared approximation the marker says not to trust. For a sparse 2x2 table an exact test exists and is cheap; for larger tables a Monte-Carlo permutation p-value would be a better lead than a flagged approximation. Today a user has to export the pair and run the exact test elsewhere. Repro: a 24-row sample with sex x a 6-level race (see the new test in tests/test proxy.py ) reports low expected: true with a chi-squared p-value only. Suggested approach: an opt-in --proxy-exact that replaces p value with scipy.stats.fisher exact for 2x2 low expected tables and with a seeded permutation estimate (fixed random state , count recorded) for larger ones…

An agent that runs it has nothing to tie the hints to the dataset it read, the alpha / correction it used, or the held out with files behind any dropped-column hint. Repro: Suggested approach: an include provenance parameter (default true, like the other two tools) that adds dataset hash , params ( alpha , correction ), overrides and proxy hints with entries via provenance.build(..., held out=...) , and a test in tests/test mcp server.py alongside the existing provenance ones.
descriptions.github:5775244775: Where: faircode/proxy.py parse held out specs() / key labels() , assets/profiler-engine.js parseHeldOut() , SPEC section 3. Current gap: 822 added PATH=COLUMN:KEY , which joins on one key column compared as exact text. Real exports often need more: a composite key ( patient id + visit date ), or keys that differ only cosmetically - " A1" vs "A1" , a1 vs A1 , 0042 vs 42 once one side was read as text. Any of those fails with "no row for N key(s)", which is correct but leaves the user to clean both files by hand. Repro: Suggested approach: accept KEY1+KEY2 for a composite key, and an opt-in normalisation ( --proxy-key-normalize , trim + casefold, and strip leading zeros on all-digit keys) applied identically to both files, in both engines and in the MCP parameter. Keep exact matching as the default and report the normalisation in provenance.

If the transaction never reached the network and the window passes, resubmitting the stored envelope is expected to be rejected as too late. The API then returns 202 on every retry, the claim stays payment pending , and the budget stays reserved. There is no route to re-prepare a payment. This is inferred from reading the code. descriptions.github:5775126877: Every image is decoded at its full size. crates/frus-image/src/lib.rs turns the bytes into full-resolution RGBA, whatever the size it will be shown at. A 12-megapixel photo shown as an 80×80 thumbnail costs 48 MB of decoded memory plus the same again as a GPU texture. A gallery of such photos is how image-heavy apps get killed for memory on low-end Android phones, and it is a common complaint about other toolkits. What exists already - An LRU decoded-image store with a byte budget in crates/frus-core/src/image.rs ( DEFAULT IMAGE CACHE BYTES = 100 MB, set image cache budget , evict over budget ). - GPU textures ( crates/frus-gpu/src/image.rs ) that are evicted when they go unused for a frame. What is missing - Decode to size. Image widgets know their laid-out size and the scale factor. They should be able to ask for a decode at that size (or a size the application sets), keyed separately…

descriptions.github:5775124339: A well-known failure of GPU-drawn toolkits is a stutter the first time an effect appears, because its shader is compiled the moment it is needed. Another is a blank or corrupted screen on low-end Android GPUs whose drivers have bugs. frus avoids the first one by design and has nothing for the second. What is missing - A pipeline cache. The warm-up cost is paid on every launch. wgpu::PipelineCache (Vulkan) can persist the compiled pipelines to disk, so the second launch skips compilation. descriptions.github:5775115425: blindbucket inspect reports what a file or a segment claims about itself — format, key id, chunk size, part index, salt, sizes — without a key. Its output is a table for people, and ADR-021 says that human-readable output is not stable: "Anything that must be parsed has --json ." keys list , gc , rotate , probe and migrate-names have it; inspect does not, and a script that wants to check the chunk size of a few thousand stored segments has nothing to parse. What to decide first A --json document is a stable interface from the release it ships in: a field is never removed, renamed, or given a different type or meaning (ADR-021). So the fields come first, in the issue or the PR description, before the code: - Numbers as numbers. chunk size in bytes and log2 chunk size , not "65536 (log2 = 16)" . - The salt in full , hex. The table shortens it for reading; a script comparing salts needs…
descriptions.github:5775115138: blindbucket probe , and every rotate and migrate-names run, ask the provider whether it enforces the conditional writes they rely on, and refuse to start where it does not (ADR-020). The step that turns the provider's answer into a verdict is classify : - no error → Ignored (the write went through despite the condition) - 412 → Enforced - any other error from the provider → Refused - no answer at all → an error, not a verdict It is pure, but internal/probe has about 11 % unit coverage, because everything around it needs a provider. A mistake here would let a rotation or a migration start against a provider that ignores the condition, which is the one outcome ADR-020 exists to prevent. descriptions.github:5775114376: A client must not be able to write the gateway's own object metadata. x-amz-meta-bb-dek , bb-kid , bb-v and the rest of docs/FORMAT.md §6.3 are what the gateway reads back to decrypt an object. mergeMetadata writes the gateway's own fields last, so most forged values would be overwritten anyway, but not a bb- field the gateway does not set on that object, and the refusal is what keeps that from being a question at all. clientMetadata is the one place that refuses them, and three write paths go through it: PutObject , CopyObject with x-amz-metadata-directive: REPLACE , and CreateMultipartUpload . Only the first is tested, and only by an integration test that skips without a running MinIO ( integration test.go , "clients may not write the reserved prefix"). Nothing asserts that the other two refuse, and a plain go test ./... does not run the check at all. What to do A unit test for…
descriptions.github:5775112960: checkCopyConditions evaluates the four x-amz-copy-source-if- headers one after another, each on its own, and refuses the copy with 412 as soon as one fails. S3 does not evaluate them independently. The CopyObject reference says, under x-amz-copy-source-if-unmodified-since : If both the x-amz-copy-source-if-match and x-amz-copy-source-if-unmodified-since headers are present in the request and evaluate as follows, Amazon S3 returns 200 OK and copies the data: - x-amz-copy-source-if-match condition evaluates to true - x-amz-copy-source-if-unmodified-since condition evaluates to false The gateway answers that request with 412 PreconditionFailed . descriptions.github:5770816381: Context Receipts and campaigns live in persistent storage with TTL EXTEND = 518 400 ledgers (about 30 days). get receipt does not extend TTL at all, and reads through RPC simulation never persist the extend ttl in get campaign . descriptions.github:5770799454: Problem. Notepad opens very large logs and text dumps. Plume reads the whole file into memory, converts it to a JS string and hands it to the editor in one go. A multi-hundred-megabyte file will freeze or crash the window, with no warning. Nothing is tested above a few megabytes. Expected fix. Measure first (open 10 MB, 50 MB, 200 MB files and record time and memory). Then add a guard: above a size threshold show a banner ("This file is 180 MB. Opening it may be slow. Open anyway / Open read-only / Cancel"), and consider a read-only chunked view for the very large case. Keep normal files unchanged. Rough sketch: Fixed looks like. Opening a 200 MB file never freezes the app: the user gets the choice, the fast path opens in a couple of seconds, and the measurements are written into docs/ so the threshold is not a guess.

descriptions.github:5770796434: Context Donation routes read live contract state and the reader already caches for 10 s, but responses carry no Cache-Control , so browsers and any CDN in front of Render refetch on every navigation. Receipts are immutable once written, so they can be cached far longer than campaigns. What to do - Set Cache-Control: public, max-age=10, stale-while-revalidate=30 on campaign, feed and stats routes. - Set a long max-age (for example one day) on GET /v1/receipts/{id} 200 responses. - Do not cache 404/503 responses. descriptions.github:5770795695: Context SorobanDonationsReader keeps a Map keyed by c: and r: that is never evicted, so memory grows with every receipt ever requested. It also has no single-flight: when the 10 s TTL expires, concurrent requests to /v1/campaigns each fire campaign count plus one get campaign simulation per campaign against the public RPC. listCampaigns also has no pagination, so the fan-out grows linearly with campaigns. What to do - Replace the Map with a small LRU (size configurable) and store pending promises so concurrent callers share one RPC read. - Add optional page / limit to GET /v1/campaigns using the existing paginated() OpenAPI helper, and only fetch the ids on the requested page. - Expose cache hit/miss counts in logs or /ready . Acceptance criteria - [ ] Cache size is bounded. - [ ] N concurrent requests after expiry cause one RPC read per key. - [ ] /v1/campaigns?page=&limit= works and…

Acceptance criteria - [ ] A campaign with older donations never renders the empty state. - [ ] Response documents…
descriptions.github:5770794391: Context The message input uses maxLength={140} , buildDonateTransaction slices to 280 characters, and the contract rejects memos whose byte length exceeds MAX TEXT LEN = 280 (Soroban String::len counts bytes). A 140 character message with emoji or non-Latin script can exceed 280 bytes and fail simulation with a generic error, and silently slicing could cut a multi-byte character in half. What to do - Validate with new TextEncoder().encode(memo).length < = 280 instead of slicing. - Show a live remaining-bytes counter linked to the input with aria-describedby . - Disable Donate and show an inline error when the limit is exceeded. Acceptance criteria - [ ] UI, lib and contract agree on one limit. - [ ] Counter is announced to screen readers. - [ ] Unit test covers a multi-byte memo near the limit. descriptions.github:5770768660: Affecting Packages/Plugins example-app example-app-legacy /cli /cli-defaults /cli-module-new /create-app e2e-test techdocs-cli-embedded-app Overview handlebars is an extension to the Mustache templating language. Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion') via the compiler's handling of pre-parsed AST objects passed to compile or precompile . When a caller supplies a hand-built or attacker-influenced AST directly to the compiler, AST node values such as path depths, path parts, literal values, content strings, hash pair keys, and block params are written into generated JavaScript code without sufficient validation, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary code into the compiled template output. The fix moves all AST value validation into the compiler itself, so that values are checked at the point they are written…
descriptions.github:5770745798: Summary Follow-up to 878. Instead of a desktop installer that edits each app's config files, ship ai-memory as a plugin/extension in each app's own marketplace , so people who live in GUI apps get capture and memory tools with a one-click install the app itself keeps up to date. This issue proposes a design and asks for feedback, and for anyone who wants to pick up an implementation. Usability is the whole point. The plugin should be as transparent as possible: install it, keep working, and memory just happens. But it must expose the setup/config knobs a real setup needs (a remote server, a token, a project override, capture exclusions) without making the default path any harder. If a user has to read docs to get the default working, the design failed. What the research found The research, including live tests, is in docs/desktop/ : start with verification-2026-10.md and extensions.md…

Expected The help message has no rustdoc syntax, and is written for the command line users. Hints - Set the help text explicitly with [value(help = "...")] on each variant, or rewrite the doc comment so that it reads well in both places. - Run cargo run -- --help to check the result. - Regenerate the completion files with just completions since they include the help text.
descriptions.github:5770434241: Overview DirsFactory::create from file in src/factory.rs calls std::env::current dir().unwrap() only to build a log message: current dir() fails when the working directory has been removed, and then the library panics instead of returning Error::NotFound . A library should not panic just for logging. Expected The error is returned without panicking, even when the working directory is unavailable. Hints - Use something like std::env::current dir().map(|d| d.display().to string()).unwrap or else(|e| format!(" ")) . - The log message also says Dirs::new from file , which is an old name; DirsFactory::create from file is the current one.
descriptions.github:5770433909: Overview build from list file in src/factory.rs throws away the error returned by File::open , and builds a new one from std::io::Error::last os error() . last os error() is not guaranteed to be the error of File::open (for example, logging may change errno ), so the error message can be wrong or misleading. Expected The actual error from File::open is returned, e.g. Hints - Keep the log message, and include the error in it. - You can check it with an unreadable file, e.g. chmod 000 list.txt; sibling list.txt .
descriptions.github:5770433418: Overview A very large --step makes sibling panic with an integer overflow. next impl in src/strategy.rs computes current + step with plain i32 addition. A debug build panics, and a release build wraps around silently. -s - with --type previous also overflows, because Previous negates the step ( -step ). Expected The command prints nothing and exits with status 1 (no more sibling directory), the same as any other out-of-range step. Hints - Use checked add / checked neg (or compute in i64 ) in src/strategy.rs , and treat an overflow as out of range. - Add test cases to the tests module in cli/main.rs (see test negative step out of range ).

descriptions.github:5769448981: Summary The repo is MPL 2.0, and that license currently covers everything including examples/ . Example code exists to be copied, and MPL's file-level copyleft makes people hesitate before lifting a snippet into their own project. The examples should be MIT so anyone can take them freely. Proposal - License everything under examples/ as MIT by adding the terms where they can't be missed ( examples/LICENSE-MIT ). - Mention it in the README next to the examples pointer, so copiers see it before they copy. Why MIT and not something else MIT is the shortest path to "just take it." Public-domain dedications raise corporate eyebrows, and dual-licensing adds paperwork nobody reads. MIT keeps attribution with zero friction, which is all we want from example code.
