descriptions.github:5694668154: The web app now has a mixer, the pen's own sound and an in-browser drawing reader. The iPad app in ios/ has none of them yet, and its Gemini prompt still follows the old rules. It's a big one, so pick a piece: - the pen's sound ( src/audio/touch.ts ) - the new prompt rules ( src/llm/planner.ts → ios/Skuzic/LLM/Planner.swift ) - the mixer ( src/ui/Mixer.tsx ) - reading the drawing on device (SigLIP 2 through Core ML) Comment with the piece you're taking so two people don't build the same thing.
descriptions.github:5694668054: The drawing reader looks at the whole page as one picture. But a drawing has more in it than what it shows: where the marks land, how fast you draw, how hard you press. Some ideas to try: - fast, scratchy strokes push Energy up; slow ones calm it down - the pen's notes sit where you draw: left on the page, left in your headphones - pressing hard brings the lead sound forward src/vision/ink.ts already turns the page into two numbers (how much ink, how warm the colours are) that nudge Energy and Brightness. That's the pattern to follow. Stroke speed and pressure are available in src/ui/DrawCanvas.tsx , and src/audio/touch.ts already measures speed for the pen's sound. Try one idea and tell us in the PR whether it made drawing feel more musical. "It didn't" is a useful answer too.
descriptions.github:5694667620: Magenta RT can be told which notes to play, frame by frame, through a 128-key piano roll. Today the bridge only uses that to hold the band to a chord loop in F major. It could follow your pen instead: a line that climbs could become a rising melody, a zigzag a trill. Where to start - server/magenta bridge.py : the Harmony class builds the notes input for every chunk. - src/ui/DrawCanvas.tsx already knows every stroke's points and timing. Open questions - Which octave, and should it stay in F major? (Probably, since the pen plays in F.) - How long should a drawn phrase keep playing after you lift the pen? - Should every stroke make a melody, or only one colour, or only when you ask? You need a Mac with Apple Silicon to run the bridge. server/README.md has the setup.
descriptions.github:5694667527: The pen's piano always plays in F major. If you change the key in the mixer (Feel → Tempo, key and more), the band moves to the new key but the pen doesn't, and they clash. The pen's notes are MIDI numbers in src/audio/touch.ts ( NOTES , and HOME for where phrases come to rest). Shifting them by the distance between F and the chosen key should be most of it. The key lives in state.config.scale (Lyria's Scale enum), so DrawCanvas needs to pass it along to the pen. Done when: pick D / Bm, draw for a bit, and the pen sounds at home with the band.
descriptions.github:5694667429: When you lift the pen, skuzic picks a mood and two instruments from a small, hand-written palette in src/vision/palette.json : 9 moods and 10 instruments. It's the easiest way to change how skuzic sounds, and you don't need to know anything about audio. Some ideas: snow, outer space, a city at night, a kalimba that only shows up for flowers. Or whatever you'd want to hear when you draw your favourite thing. How 1. Add an entry to palette.json . A mood needs a short prompt ("hushed and starlit") and a few tags describing drawings it should match ("a crescent moon", "a starry night sky"). An instrument needs a prompt ("gentle harp arpeggios") and its own tags. 2. Run scripts/embed-palette.py (the command is at the top of the file). pnpm test fails until you do, on purpose. 3. Draw something that should trigger it. The mixer's History tab tells you what it heard ("Feels like rain: felt…
descriptions.github:5694581191: Context Agent.run() returns a Report whose steps hold the exact prompt, the raw response and each action's verdict. Nothing records what a step cost . Proposal (open to discussion) - Let an adapter report usage without breaking custom models. One option is an optional last usage attribute that the agent reads after each call. Another is letting complete() return a str subclass that carries the usage. Please propose a design in a comment before…

descriptions.github:5694580973: Context When a belief cites a document, Corollary checks that the quote actually states the value, at the scale its unit says. For example, 4.3e9 matches "$4.3 billion" and "$4.3B", but not "$4 million". The provenance check uses the same matching. The units are English only. A Brazilian or Spanish filing that says "receita de 4.3 bilhões" doesn't match 4.3e9 , so kb.cite() raises CitationError on a correct citation. What to do In src/corollary/textmatch.py , add these words to UNIT and UNIT SCALES , in singular and plural, with and without accents: | Word | Scale | |---|---| | mil | thousand ( 1e-3 ) | | milhão / milhões , millón / millones | million ( 1e-6 ) | | bilhão / bilhões | billion ( 1e-9 ) | | trilhão / trilhões , billón / billones | trillion ( 1e-12 ) | Note that Spanish billón means 10^12, not 10^9. Spanish "mil millones" (10^9) and decimal commas ("4,3") are out of scope…

Share the logic through /server-shared so all adapters behave the same, and update the OpenAPI description there. This touches several packages, so please comment here…

descriptions.github:5694316881: Quail refuses ORDER BY, OFFSET, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, and plain column predicates in WHERE. Users apply them on the client or in the source database. Semantic top-k, the most wanted query, cannot be written: Plan Three PRs, grouped by the machinery they share. Everything runs on the coordinator in Arrow; the GPU executor changes only where noted. Only the Quail planners (standard and reranker) get new nodes. The stock vLLM and SGLang planners refuse the new clauses, so a query with one runs on Quail only. PR 1: ordering and the limit rule. 187. ORDER BY, OFFSET, top-k, and DISTINCT, since all four are fields on the root Project and one coordinator node. - Sort keys, offset, and a distinct flag become fields on the root Project, beside LIMIT. - One Sort node: select-k when there is a LIMIT, full sort otherwise. DISTINCT is an Acero aggregate with no functions in the same node. - Limit…

descriptions.github:5694218948: Description avenx stats prints every compiler diagnostic twice. No other command that compiles does. With one undeclared template reference in a project: bin/commands/stats.js compiles the project twice. It calls buildModel(cli) at line 92, which compiles and reports diagnostics, and then re-runs the parser per file to measure compiled template size: extractTemplate re-runs template validation, so every warning is reported a second time. The comment above that block says it collects things "the way compileUnit collects it, so the validation sees" the same inputs — the duplication is a side effect of that deliberate second pass, and it went unnoticed. Besides the doubled output, it means avenx stats does roughly twice the compile work it needs to. Reproduction Goal avenx stats should report each diagnostic once. Suggested implementation Two routes, and it is worth looking at both before…
descriptions.github:5694215877: Found in a post-merge review of 93 (issue 76). rootCmd sets neither SilenceUsage nor SilenceErrors , so cobra prints: The message itself is clear, which is what the CHANGELOG claims, so this is cosmetic — but this is the second time a bad CLI argument produces a confusing screen (the first was the same port flag, before 93 validated it). Definition of done: - SilenceUsage: true on webCmd (or the root), so a runtime flag error is not followed by the full help - decide explicitly whether SilenceErrors stays off (the error is then printed once, by cobra, and os.Exit still gets a non-zero code) and note the choice in the code - a test asserting an invalid port does not print "Usage:" — or a short manual note in AGENTS.md if this is not testable in the current CLI test setup - bin/lint.sh green
descriptions.github:5694215001: Description A reference to an AVX PUBLIC variable that has no value is replaced with the literal undefined and nothing says so. replaceEnvVariables in lib/env.js : So a typo — process.env.AVX PUBLIC API URLL — compiles to undefined , the build reports success, and the application receives undefined wherever it expected a URL. The failure surfaces later as a fetch to undefined/users or a blank value in the UI, with nothing connecting it back to the misspelled variable. A forgotten .env entry in CI produces the same thing, which is the case where it costs the most: the build that was supposed to catch it is the build that silently shipped it. The compiler has a diagnostic for exactly this shape of problem elsewhere — AVX W03 for an undeclared template reference, AVX W40 for state nothing reads — but nothing for an environment variable that was referenced and never set. descriptions.github:5694214853: Found in a post-merge review of 93 (issue 76). validatePort rejects 0 ( n < 1 ). Before that change, tokeneks web --port 0 bound an ephemeral port and started serving normally — the printed URL was wrong ( but the command worked. Rejecting 0 is the right call for a CLI that prints a URL built from the flag, so this is not a defect — it is an unlisted behaviour change on a public flag. CHANGELOG.md says only that out-of-range ports now error. Definition of done: - CHANGELOG notes that port 0 is rejected, and why (the dashboard prints the URL it was given, so an ephemeral port is useless to the user) - one clause, same style as the existing entry

descriptions.github:5694213737: Found in a post-merge review of 93 (issue 76). validatePort has exactly one caller, and the test exercises only the helper. Two mutations both leave the suite green: 1. delete the if err := validatePort(port) block from runWeb → TestValidatePort still passes 2. move that block below openTokeneksStore() ( web.go:227 ) → still passes, and now a bad flag leaks a store handle and starts the watcher before failing What 76 asked for is fail-fast before the store opens , and nothing pins that. Where to start: web test.go . descriptions.github:5694130790: The English reads "brought forward no sacrifice for sins", which inverts Hebrews 10:12. The printed Greek has οὐδεμίαν, which is probably a corruption of οὗτος δὲ μίαν ("but this one [offered] one sacrifice"). Details: docs/FIDELITY ISSUES 20261003.md. Book: books/cyril-alexandria-adoration-1 How to fix: check another witness (another edition or manuscript reading) for this line, and translate it with the emendation marked if the witness supports it. Cite the witness in the pull request.
descriptions.github:5694130618: The English of the Origen Romans catena paraphrases the Greek and adds words it does not have, for example "through faith alone" (no μόνη in the Greek), εὐσέβειαν rendered "security" (it is "piety"), and "as if He arbitrarily chose some and rejected others" (not in the Greek). Details: docs/FIDELITY ISSUES 20261003.md. Book: books/origen-romans-catena How to fix: retranslate from the locked Greek following docs/START HERE.md. Do not copy any existing English translation.

descriptions.github:5693457949: Description In ExecutionProperties.java , bufferTimeout is annotated with: In Apache Flink ( ExecutionOptions.BUFFER TIMEOUT ), setting buffer-timeout to -1 (or -1ms ) is a standard and officially documented tuning mechanism: - buffer-timeout: 0 = Low latency mode; buffers are flushed immediately after each record, reducing throughput. - buffer-timeout: 100ms = Periodic flushing every 100ms. - buffer-timeout: -1 = Maximum throughput mode; periodic flushing is disabled, and network buffers are only transmitted when full. Because (millis = 0) rejects any duration with negative milliseconds, Flinkboot prevents operators from configuring buffer-timeout: -1 , making it impossible to enable maximum-throughput streaming execution via typed properties. descriptions.github:5693456809: Description In RestoreMode.java , RestoreMode.LEGACY is currently included as an option: In Apache Flink (since Flink 1.15), RestoreMode.LEGACY has been deprecated due to state ownership ambiguities: - Under LEGACY mode, Flink did not maintain clear file ownership between the original savepoint and newly taken checkpoints, risking silent state corruption if operators moved or deleted the original savepoint while the restored job was running. - Apache Flink strongly advises using NO CLAIM (default, safe: Flink leaves the original savepoint untouched and creates independent checkpoint files) or CLAIM (Flink assumes ownership of savepoint files). - Furthermore, RestoreMode.LEGACY is completely removed in Flink 2.0. Eliminating LEGACY now in milestone before the 1.0.0 release ensures users do not rely on an unsafe and obsolete mode. Expected Behavior 1. In RestoreMode.java , remove the…
descriptions.github:5693450673: Every parcel tracked so far came back with a single status, so the opt-in status history only ever holds the latest step. It is not known whether ICS Courier ever returns earlier steps for a parcel that is still on its way. What would help: if you track a parcel that is still in transit, turn on the status history and say in a comment whether it ever shows more than one entry, and how that compares with the steps on the ICS Courier tracking page. Please leave out tracking numbers, names and addresses.
descriptions.github:5693450510: ICS Courier reports the time of a status without a time zone. The integration assumes it is Canadian local time and shows it as received, so the delivered time may be off by a few hours depending on where you and the parcel are. What would help: compare the delivered time on the parcel sensor with the time on the ICS Courier tracking page, and say in a comment which province the parcel was delivered in and whether the two match. Please leave out tracking numbers, names and addresses.
descriptions.github:5693450302: So far only delivered parcels have been tracked, so the only status confirmed on a real parcel is delivered . Everything before that — picked up, in transit, out for delivery, a missed delivery, a parcel held at a depot — has not been seen yet and shows as unknown . The integration logs a one-shot WARNING starting with Unrecognised ICS Courier status whenever it meets a status it doesn't know. That line holds only ICS Courier's short status code. What would help: when you see that warning, paste the line into a comment here, together with what the ICS Courier tracking page said about the parcel at that moment. Please leave out tracking numbers, names and addresses.

descriptions.github:5693371408: Description In Apache Flink (since 1.13), the runtime state backend and checkpoint storage are decoupled into two distinct concerns: 1. State Backend : Manages in-flight working state during execution ( HashMapStateBackend , EmbeddedRocksDBStateBackend ). Configured via env.setStateBackend(...) . 2. Checkpoint Storage : Manages where and how durable snapshots are persisted ( JobManagerCheckpointStorage , FileSystemCheckpointStorage ). Configured via env.getCheckpointConfig().setCheckpointStorage(...) . Currently in Flinkboot: - checkpoint-storage is declared inside StateBackendProperties.java ( state-backend.checkpoint-storage ). - storage-uri is declared inside CheckpointingProperties.java ( checkpointing.storage-uri ). If only initial-backoff is specified (e.g. initial-backoff: 5m ), Flink applies its default max-backoff of 2m . At runtime, Flink throws IllegalArgumentException: initialBackoff cannot be greater than maxBackoff during environment initialization. 2. If only max-backoff is specified (e.g. max-backoff: 500ms ), Flink applies its default initial-backoff of 1s . At runtime, Flink throws IllegalArgumentException: initialBackoff cannot be greater than maxBackoff . Hardcoding Flink defaults into Flinkboot is fragile against upstream drift across Flink versions. Therefore, the robust fail-fast invariant is: If either initial-backoff or max-backoff is…

descriptions.github:5693246631: Description In Apache Flink's checkpointing architecture, min-pause-between-checkpoints specifies a mandatory rest duration between the completion of checkpoint $N$ and the triggering of checkpoint $N+1$. Concurrently, max-concurrent-checkpoints specifies how many checkpoints can be in-flight simultaneously. These two settings are mutually incompatible when min-pause-between-checkpoints 0 and max-concurrent-checkpoints 1 : Flink cannot trigger concurrent checkpoints while simultaneously enforcing a mandatory pause between them. Apache Flink enforces this invariant and throws an IllegalArgumentException at startup: Currently, CheckpointingPropertiesValidator does not validate this interdependency. If an operator sets both min-pause-between-checkpoints: 5s and max-concurrent-checkpoints: 2 , Flinkboot validation passes, only for Flink to fail at job startup. Expected Behavior In…

In multi-parallelism deployments, this causes: 1. JMX MBean name collisions ( InstanceAlreadyExistsException in Kafka metrics reporting). 2. descriptions.github:5692966647: A client sending a valid handshake with Upgrade: WebSocket (RFC 6455 section 4.2.1 says the value is case-insensitive) makes CanWorkWith return false, because the value is compared with == "websocket" . The handshake is never tried and the request falls through to normal HTTP handling, usually a 404. The Connection check on the same line is already case-insensitive. Location: MaxLib.WebServer/WebSocket/WebSocketService.cs:35-40 Fix: Compare with string.Equals(..., "websocket", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) .
descriptions.github:5692965880: WebServiceGroup.Clear() empties Services but does not unsubscribe Service PriorityChanged from the former members, unlike Remove and WebServiceCollection.Clear() . A cleared service that later changes its own Priority fires the handler, which re-inserts it into the cleared group, so it runs again on later requests. The group also stays referenced by every cleared service. Location: MaxLib.WebServer/WebServiceGroup.cs:67-70 Fix: Unsubscribe PriorityChanged from every service in Clear() before clearing, as WebServiceCollection.Clear() does.
descriptions.github:5692965646: SetSessionCookie casts MaxAge.TotalSeconds to int unchecked. A MaxAge above about 68 years (for example TimeSpan.FromDays(365 100) ) emits Max-Age=- on net8.0, so the browser deletes the session cookie immediately, while Expires stays correct. A much larger MaxAge makes DateTime.UtcNow + MaxAge throw. Location: MaxLib.WebServer/Sessions/SessionServiceBase.cs:132 Fix: Clamp the value to int.MaxValue before the cast and clamp the Expires computation to DateTime.MaxValue (or validate MaxAge in its setter).
descriptions.github:5692964597: An app sets MultipartFormData.StorageMapper for encryption at rest and receives an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body over UrlEncodedData.MaximumCacheSize (50 MB). The whole raw body is copied in plaintext to a temp FileStream that never passes through StorageMapper , while multipart parts, RawPostData and the per-value spill do use it. Location: MaxLib.WebServer/Post/UrlEncodedData.cs:104-113 Fix: Wrap rawFile with MultipartFormData.StorageMapper?.Invoke(task, file) ?? file like the other temp-file writes.
descriptions.github:5692963969: MultipartFormData matches parameter and token names case-sensitively, but RFC 9110/2045 make them case-insensitive. Content-Type: multipart/form-data; Boundary=xyz does not match boundaryRegex (no IgnoreCase ), so the valid body is rejected with 400. A part with Content-Disposition: Form-Data; name="a" fails StartsWith("form-data", Ordinal) and becomes a plain FormEntry , losing its name and filename. Location: MaxLib.WebServer/Post/MultipartFormData.cs ( boundaryRegex() , and the disposition check near line 119) Fix: Add RegexOptions.IgnoreCase | RegexOptions.CultureInvariant to boundaryRegex() and compare the disposition type with StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase .
descriptions.github:5692963773: Content-Type: multipart/form-data ; boundary=x (optional whitespace before ; , allowed by RFC 9110) leaves MimeType as "multipart/form-data " with a trailing space. The DataHandler lookup misses, and the body is stored as RawPostData instead of being parsed as multipart. Handlers that expect MultipartFormData or UrlEncodedData silently get no data. Location: MaxLib.WebServer/HttpPost.cs:40-60 Fix: Trim the media type (and the parameter part) after splitting at ; , before the DataHandler lookup.
descriptions.github:5692963103: On the public SpanStream , Seek(-2, SeekOrigin.End) moves to Length instead of Length - 2 because it uses Math.Max where Math.Min is needed. Setting Position = Length throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException although Stream allows that position. Currently only NetworkReader uses it and never seeks, so only direct users hit this. Location: MaxLib.WebServer/IO/SpanStream.cs:87-100 , MaxLib.WebServer/IO/SpanStream.cs:27-36 Fix: Use Math.Max(0, Math.Min(Length, Length + offset)) for SeekOrigin.End and accept value == Memory.Length in the Position setter.

What we'd like Footnotes rendered the usual way: a small link in the text, the notes at the end, and a link back from each note. descriptions.github:5692957504: Description Nothing checks that the needs: lists in the GitHub Actions workflows match the jobs that exist. ci-ok aggregates needs: [...] by hand: Removing a job and forgetting its entry here is silent. GitHub does not fail a workflow because a needs: entry names a job that does not exist; the aggregate simply stops waiting for it (or the workflow is invalid and only shows up in the run log). No test in the repository reads .github/workflows/ — the suites are PHP only ( tests/Unit , tests/Integration ) — so a mismatch is caught by a human reading the diff, if at all. It bit us while removing the build-piper-musl job ( 26): the job and its needs: entry had to be removed together, in two files, in the same PR. Where to start - .github/workflows/ci.yml ( ci-ok job) and .github/workflows/release.yml ( publish job). - Add a unit test, for example tests/Unit/WorkflowTest.php , that parses…

descriptions.github:5692854913: Some shipments are sent as one consignment made up of several parcels. The integration doesn't track those yet: such a code shows as unknown , and the integration logs a one-shot WARNING starting with Poczta Polska returned a grouped consignment . What would help: if you see that warning, comment here with how many parcels the shipment had and what the Poczta Polska tracking page showed for it, for example whether each parcel had its own status. Please leave out tracking numbers, names and addresses.
descriptions.github:5692854548: Every status seen on real parcels so far maps to a canonical status: posted, in transit, customs, out for delivery, a delivery notice, waiting at the post office, returned, delivered and collected. The rarer outcomes have not appeared on a tracked parcel yet, such as a refused or undeliverable item or a delivery attempt that failed for another reason. Some of those are mapped as problem without having been seen live, and anything else shows as unknown . The integration logs a one-shot WARNING starting with Unrecognised Poczta Polska status whenever it meets a status code it doesn't know. That line holds only the status code. What would help: when you see that warning, paste the line into a comment here, together with what the Poczta Polska tracking page or app said about the parcel at that moment. If a parcel shows as problem while the tracking page says something more specific, that is…

descriptions.github:5692051383: On windows-latest , npm test starts and never finishes; runs sat for hours until cancelled. macOS and Linux pass on Node 22 and 24. CI now fails a test that runs longer than 60 seconds ( --test-timeout=60000 ) and a job after 20 minutes, so the next Windows run should name the test that hangs. Likely suspects are tests that start child processes or the local named-pipe bridge and don't close them on Windows. Windows is experimental (see 28), so this doesn't fail the build, but fixing it is the first step to supporting it.

I ran into one small fault and believe I have found the cause, so I wanted to pass it along. Symptom On my home PC (Windows, keyboard plugged directly into the motherboard), the Num Lock, Caps Lock, and Scroll Lock LEDs went dark after roughly 30 to 60 minutes of normal use. The PC had not gone to sleep and the keys kept working. Pressing the lock keys still changed the state in Windows, but the LEDs stayed dark. Unplugging the keyboard, or pressing a key mapped to QK REBOOT, brought them back. The solenoid was off. The fault did not appear on my work computer over a full day. descriptions.github:5691839656: Problem BarChart, PieChart, and Legend support updating their content after construction. However, updates made after calling add to page() do not update the objects stored on that page. The internal group contains the replacement objects, while the page still contains the original objects. Consequently, exporting the page produces a diagram with stale data, labels, or colors. Calling add to page() again is not a reliable workaround: it adds the replacement objects without removing the old content. Reproduction The same behavior was reproduced with: PieChart.update data(): the page retains the original slices and labels. Legend.update mapping(): the page retains the original color boxes and labels. Color updates also use the same rebuild mechanism and therefore have the same underlying problem. Root cause add to page() adds each object from the internal group to the page. When an update…

descriptions.github:5691730227: Problem you're trying to solve Organisations on Google Workspace keep Word, PowerPoint, and Excel files in Google Drive. OfficeAgent can only reach files on a local disk or in SharePoint/OneDrive, so those teams have to copy files out and back by hand. Scope Office files stored in Drive ( .docx , .pptx , .xlsx ) are in scope. descriptions.github:5691531338: Every tweet is sent to the model each time it is seen. The service worker caches verdicts for the session, but the cache is lost when the browser restarts, so tweets that reappear later cost another API call. Idea: persist verdicts in chrome.storage.local , keyed by tweet ID plus a hash of the active filters, strictness and model settings, with an expiry and a size cap. Things to think about: - Invalidate when filters, threshold, model or provider change. - Keep the cache bounded so storage doesn't grow forever. - Don't cache failed calls. - Don't store more tweet text than needed. Storing only the verdict is enough. This is a bigger change than the other open issues. Please comment with your approach before starting. Where to look: the caching code in background.js and the decisions map in content.js .

descriptions.github:5689993370: call() 's typed overload takes returns: type[T] . Literal[...] (and X | None ) are special forms, not types, so mypy and Pyright fall through to the overload that returns Any . doesn't have this gap, because the return annotation is read from the function itself. Possible directions: - PEP 747 TypeForm , imported only under TYPE CHECKING , since thunc can't take a runtime dependency on typing extensions - Extra overloads for the common cases Requirements: any fix has to pass mypy --strict thunc and Pyright, and must not change runtime behaviour. A small file of reveal type / assert type checks would make the result easy to verify.

descriptions.github:5689993072: Right now every call goes to the model, so re-running a script costs the same every time, and tests that use a real model aren't reproducible. Wanted: - Cache: identical calls (same backend, model, system prompt and prompt text) return the stored answer. - Record/replay: record a run's answers, then replay them, for example in CI, failing loudly on any call that wasn't recorded. Open design questions (please discuss here before writing code): - How is it switched on? thunc.configure(cache="...") , an env var, a context manager? - Where does it store answers? A directory of JSON files is easy to diff and commit. - Should a cached answer still be parsed and ensure= -checked? Probably yes. - How does it interact with trace= ? Where: thunc/core.py ( send is the single point every call goes through) and thunc/config.py . It must stay standard-library only.
descriptions.github:5689992935: Allow a Pydantic model as a return type, next to dataclasses: Constraint: thunc's core uses the standard library only, so Pydantic must not become a dependency. Where: thunc/schema.py - describe() : describe the fields, possibly from model json schema() . - validate() : call model validate(value) and turn a ValidationError into a ValueError with a short message. That message is sent back to the model on retry. Tests: offline only, in tests/test schema.py . Pydantic can be a dev-only dependency, or the tests can skip when it isn't installed. Please comment with the approach before opening a large PR.

descriptions.github:5689715095: What The nl pack masks Dutch BTW-ids as vat id . Add the German counterpart to the de pack: the Umsatzsteuer-Identifikationsnummer (USt-IdNr). It identifies sole traders, so it can be personal data. Examples: DE136695976 , DE . Format - DE followed by 9 digits; the first digit is never 0 . - Spaces or dots between groups are common ( DE ). - The 9th digit is a check digit (ISO 7064 MOD 11,10): product = 10 ; for each of the first 8 digits, sum = (digit + product) mod 10 , if sum == 0: sum = 10 , product = (2 sum) mod 11 . The check digit is (11 - product) mod 10 . Spec: BZSt: Aufbau der USt-IdNr. Watch out for - Require an uppercase DE and a non-word boundary before it, so words and identifiers that end in de are not touched. - Look at how nl vat detector handles the NL format in all three backends and keep the structure parallel. Category Reuse vat id , so no new type is needed. Where…

descriptions.github:5689712228: Description BinaryFileResponseStrategy::scheduleFileCleanup() ( src/Http/Response/Strategy/BinaryFileResponseStrategy.php ) sets $connection- onBufferDrain to delete the temp file after the send. For a file of 2 MB or more, Workerman Http::sendStream() ( vendor/workerman/workerman/src/Protocols/Http.php ) replaces onBufferDrain with its own callback and sets it to null at the end. So the cleanup callback is lost, and the file is deleted only when the connection closes (the onClose fallback). On a keep-alive connection the temp file can stay on disk for a long time. This was found while working on issue 899 (PR 950). It is not tested yet. descriptions.github:5689712052: Description The timeout sweeper in src/Worker/ServerWorker.php (around line 141) calls $connection- close() on a connection that stopped. In Workerman 5.2.2, close() with a non-empty send buffer only sets STATUS CLOSING and stops reading ( vendor/workerman/workerman/src/Connection/TcpConnection.php:985-991 ). If the client never reads, destroy() is never called. The socket, the send buffer and the file handle from Http::sendStream() stay open until the worker stops. This is an old problem. It was seen in review of PR 950 (issue 899). A slow-reader client can use it to hold sockets and file handles. descriptions.github:5689427317: Problem Description In lib/state.js , writeJsonAtomic performs a write to a temporary file followed by fs.renameSync(temporaryPath, filePath) . On Windows, background file indexing services, antivirus scanners, or active IDE file watchers (like VS Code) can hold a transient read lock on filePath for a few milliseconds, occasionally causing fs.renameSync to throw an EPERM or EBUSY error. Expected Behavior Atomic writes should be resilient to momentary Windows file locks by attempting up to 3 retries with a small backoff before throwing. Proposed Solution & Implementation Hints In lib/state.js : Relevant Files - lib/state.js - tests/test-flow.js Acceptance Criteria - [ ] Atomic writes retry gracefully on transient Windows locks. - [ ] Existing atomic persistence unit tests continue to pass.

descriptions.github:5689404678: pkg/owasp/vector.go:97 sets IntrusionDetection: 9 - vul . On OWASP's scale not logged is 9, meaning higher likelihood. At ta=7, vul=6, tech=bus=7 the published score is 6.5 x 7 = 45.5 , while recomputing the 8-factor mean from the published vector gives 51/8 = 6.125 , so 42.875 . descriptions.github:5687853572: Individual agents and validators have unit tests, but there is no test that runs the Research Mode graph from problem statement to final paper. What to build An offline integration test that runs the compiled graph in backend/app/graph/research mode builder.py with a fake LLM that returns canned structured output, mocked provider adapters returning a few PaperRecord s, and the human-review interrupts resumed programmatically. Assert that the PRISMA invariants hold and that the final state contains a paper, a claims manifest, and a validation report. Notes This is a larger task. Existing tests in tests/test retrieval and graph.py and tests/test research mode.py show how parts of the graph are already exercised.
descriptions.github:5687853367: frontend/app.js is the whole app UI in vanilla JS with no build step, and it has no tests. A change can break the stage list, the SSE handling, or the checkpoint panels without anything noticing. What to build Smoke tests with Playwright (or a similar tool) against a local server with the backend mocked: the page loads without console errors, a mocked SSE stream advances the stages, and a checkpoint panel renders and submits. Notes Keep it out of the default pytest run if it needs browsers, and add a separate CI job. Please comment your approach before starting.
descriptions.github:5687852898: Tests marked live hit the real academic APIs and are deselected by default ( pytest.ini ), so nothing runs them. Provider adapters can break when an upstream API changes and nobody finds out. What to build A GitHub Actions workflow with workflow dispatch and a weekly cron that runs pytest -m live . It should read any needed emails or keys from repository secrets, skip providers whose secrets are missing, and report failures without blocking pull requests. Notes Keep request volume low to respect rate limits and polite-pool rules (see .env.example ).

What to build Replace that dependency. Options: - implement a small SQLite-backed BaseCache against langchain-core directly, or - use a maintained standalone cache package. Acceptance - No deprecation warning on import. - Existing tests pass, plus a test for cache hit, miss, and persistence across instances.

Optionally flag untagged sentences that contain numbers, comparisons, or citations so the writer or the reviewer sees them. Notes - Tag instructions are in backend/app/agents/research mode/writing.py ; the tag-to-claim conversion is claims linker node . - Do not claim full coverage anywhere in the UI or docs. descriptions.github:5687850317: Claims are extracted per sentence. A sentence with two clauses and one citation counts as a single claim, so the second clause is never checked on its own. What to build Split compound sentences into clause-level claims before they are linked to evidence, for example on semicolons and coordinating conjunctions, while keeping the citation attached to the clause it belongs to. A simple rule-based splitter is fine as a first version. Notes - The claims manifest is built in claims linker node in backend/app/agents/research mode/writing.py . - Claim IDs are deterministic ( {section} cl001 ). Splitting must keep them stable and unique. - Add tests with multi-clause sentences, abbreviations ("et al.", "e.g."), and decimals, which must not trigger a split.
descriptions.github:5687850114: validate citations in text in backend/app/agents/research mode/validation.py resolves an in-text citation by matching only the first-author surname and the year against the corpus. Problem - Two papers by the same first author in the same year are indistinguishable. - Surnames with particles, hyphens, or diacritics (de la Cruz, Müller/Mueller) can fail to match. - A wrong citation that happens to share a surname and year counts as resolved. What to build A stricter match, for example adding the second author or title tokens when available, handling a / b year suffixes, and normalising diacritics. Keep the current behaviour as the fallback so existing reports do not regress. Acceptance - New unit tests cover same-author-same-year ambiguity, diacritics, and suffixes. - Existing validation tests still pass.

descriptions.github:5687584257: The order object has several time fields for the delivery window. Their unit and timezone are unconfirmed, so the integration deliberately leaves planned from and planned to empty and does not claim the delivery window capability. sensor.airmee next delivery therefore stays unknown , and the Deliveries calendar has nothing to place. Timestamps are currently accepted only as Unix seconds in a plausible range; anything else is refused with a one-shot warning rather than guessed at. What would help: a diagnostics export from a parcel with a known delivery window. Comparing the raw numbers against what the Airmee app showed you settles the unit and timezone in one go, and then these fields can be switched on.
descriptions.github:5687583859: Airmee's order object carries its status in two places: a machine-readable code per timeline event, and a human-readable text field. The integration prefers the code, and only falls back to mapping the text when the code is absent — the text is localized and ambiguous, so the fallback deliberately maps only unmistakable wordings. Which of the two the tracking-link route actually returns has never been seen on a real response. The account route is expected to carry both. descriptions.github:5687540452: The Structural Health Monitoring section has six entries and all of them are modal analysis tools (operational or experimental modal analysis and camera based displacement measurement). The section note already says it is thin. The concrete gaps are: - Damage detection and anomaly detection on vibration or strain data. - Sensor data pipelines : acquisition, cleaning and storage of long term monitoring data. - Benchmark datasets from instrumented bridges or buildings, which would also fit Open Datasets. - Fatigue and remaining life assessment tools. descriptions.github:5687540276: Crack and surface defect detection is one of the most common uses of machine learning in civil engineering, and the AI and Machine Learning section currently has no project for it. The two entries that used to cover it, DeepCrack and crack segmentation, were removed in 10 because neither repository has a license, and DeepCrack restricts its data to non commercial use. SDNET2018 in Open Datasets provides images, but there is no listed model or training code. What is needed A project for crack or defect segmentation or detection on concrete, asphalt or steel surfaces that: - has an explicit open source license for the code, - states the license or terms of any bundled dataset or weights, - documents how to run inference or training. Suggestions as comments or pull requests are welcome.
descriptions.github:5687540106: The Learning Resources section covers GIS, geotechnical engineering, hydraulics and general engineering computation, but has nothing for three areas the list itself is strong in: - Earthquake engineering : course notes or worked notebooks on response spectra, ground motion processing, hazard or nonlinear time history analysis. - Structural dynamics : open textbooks or notebooks on single and multi degree of freedom systems and modal analysis. - BIM and IFC : tutorials for IfcOpenShell, openBIM workflows or IFC data handling. Candidates that were looked at and rejected because the repository has no license: the DOLFINx tutorial and seismo-live. A resource needs an explicit open license (code or content, for example MIT or CC BY) and enough documentation to follow without the lecture it was written for. Suggestions as comments or pull requests are welcome.

That works between people who meet, but an organisation (a bank, a newsroom, a public figure) needs a way for anyone to find its key. The spec marks this TBD . Candidates to compare: - A well-known HTTPS path on the organisation's domain ( /.well-known/voxtrust ), like security.txt . - A DNS TXT record, possibly with DNSSEC. - Key transparency logs, so a swapped key is visible. - Reusing an existing system (C2PA trust lists, WebFinger, Keybase-style proofs). What matters: a verifier must be able to tell a key that rotated legitimately from one an attacker swapped, and the answer must work offline after the first lookup. Comments with prior art and trade-offs are very welcome before any spec text is written.
descriptions.github:5685536907: C2PA Content Credentials are becoming the standard for signed media provenance. File mode is close to it in spirit (a signed manifest inside the file), and a bridge would let C2PA-aware tools show a Vox Trust seal (roadmap, phase 6). Open questions, a design note answering them is a great first contribution: - Should the VOXT manifest become a custom C2PA assertion, or should Vox Trust per-chunk digests map onto C2PA's existing hashing of media? - C2PA signs with X.509 certificates; Vox Trust uses bare Ed25519 keys pinned by contacts. How do the two trust models coexist? - What does a verifier show when the C2PA signature and the Vox Trust seal disagree? Prototype with the c2pa Rust crate. Please start with a short design note (a markdown file in docs/decisions/ ) before a large PR.

descriptions.github:5685536145: The core already implements the pairing text of spec section 9 ( vox trust core::pairing , with encode and decode ), but the command-line tool cannot produce or read one. Today you share a public key as 64 hex characters. Proposal: - vox-trust pubkey KEYFILE --pairing [LABEL] prints voxtrust:0:public: < 64 hex [: ] . - vox-trust verify FILE --pin also accepts a pairing text (or a file containing one) besides a bare hex key. - Circle pairing texts contain the secret, so the CLI must never print one unless asked explicitly, and the help text should say why. Where: crates/vox-trust-cli/src/main.rs (argument parsing and the USAGE text), tests in crates/vox-trust-cli/tests/ . Keep the existing exit codes. A CHANGELOG entry under [Unreleased] is welcome.

descriptions.github:5684982544: Summary With hooks.transparent prefixes = ["sudo", "sudo -E"] , rtk discover counts sudo RTK DISABLED=1 docker ps and RTK DISABLED=1 sudo docker ps as bypasses ( 3808), but not the same lines with an expanded value: rtk rewrite "sudo docker ps" rewrites under that config, so dropping the assignment would recover the savings. Cause strip disabled prefix for analytics ( src/discover/registry.rs ) walks raw lexer::tokenize tokens, which split one shell word at $ : RTK DISABLED=$CI is two tokens, RTK DISABLED= and $CI . The walk treats $CI as the command word, finds it unsupported, and falls back to strip disabled prefix , which does not peel sudo . Walking coalesced words ( lexer::coalesce words , as without rtk disabled in src/discover/mod.rs does) would keep the assignment whole. A missed count, not a wrong one: develop does not count these lines either. Related: 3756, 3808.

A 500 or 413 response resolves normally, so those entries are dropped without any signal. 2. descriptions.github:5684207567: What is wrong No handler or middleware limits the request body size. json.NewDecoder(r.Body) reads whatever arrives. With auth on and --bind 0.0.0.0 , an authenticated client can make the server buffer an arbitrarily large body. What we want Add http.MaxBytesReader in the middleware chain that already wraps every route. 1 MiB is far more than any request body the API takes. An oversized body answers 413 as problem+json through respondError . descriptions.github:5684207074: What is wrong run.( Engine).Submit checks ActiveRunForLock and then calls CreateRun as two separate statements. The index on runs.lock key is not unique, so two submits that land between those calls both succeed. That can happen with two UI requests, or the CLI in one terminal and the UI in another. Two runs then hold one lock, which is exactly what ADR-0004 exists to prevent. What we want Make the check and the insert one atomic statement, so it also holds across processes: Report zero rows affected as the LockConflictError . The alternative is a partial unique index on lock key WHERE status IN (…) AND lock key != '' , which needs a migration. Where to look - src/internal/run/engine.go ( Submit ) - src/internal/store/runs.go ( CreateRun , ActiveRunForLock ) - src/internal/store/migrations/ if you take the index route Definition of done - [ ] A test submits the same lock key…
descriptions.github:5684206511: What is wrong labctl never installs a signal handler, so cmd.Context() is context.Background() and Ctrl-C kills the process with Go's default action. Scripts started through internal/toolchain run in their own process group ( Setpgid ), so the terminal's SIGINT does not reach them. They keep running with no parent, and their run stays running until the next engine start reconciles it. That breaks the promise in ADR-0003. Two smaller effects of the same gap: - labctl ui exits without calling Shutdown on the HTTP server. - scenario verify --watch sleeps with time.Sleep , which no context can interrupt. What we want - In cli.Execute , run the root command under signal.NotifyContext(ctx, os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM) via rootCmd.ExecuteContext . Everything already reads cmd.Context() , so cancellation flows to run.Engine and each process group gets its graceful SIGTERM. - labctl ui calls…
descriptions.github:5684205957: What is wrong Engine.Get returns the Scenario held in the engine's cache, but only after setting s.Active on it. Any two goroutines that call Get at the same time, or one that calls Get while a run reads the scenario, race on that field. - go test -race ./internal/service/scenario/ reports it on main in TestActivate ConflictsPerScenario , which fails most runs. - The race is also live in labctl ui , because its HTTP handlers call Get concurrently. What we want Stop writing to the cached value. Return a shallow copy with Active filled in, so every caller stays the same. (Dropping the field in favour of IsActive(name) is the alternative, but it touches every caller; take the copy approach first.) Where to look - src/internal/scenario/engine.go ( Get , isActive ) - src/internal/service/scenario/ for the failing test Definition of done - [ ] Get never mutates the cached scenario. - [ ] A…

descriptions.github:5684142376: The README says to put RiffPlayer behind a reverse proxy with HTTPS when exposing it to the internet, but gives no examples — that's where many people get stuck. Acceptance criteria - [ ] You actually tried the examples (with a real domain, or localhost + a self-signed cert) and noted which versions you used. - [ ] Settings that matter for audio streaming (large bodies / long timeouts / buffering), if any, are mentioned.
descriptions.github:5684142179: Problem A: In Admin → Users → "Change pw", leaving the field empty and pressing Save sends the request. The server silently ignores an empty password ( if (password) ), but the UI closes the editor as if it had been saved. Problem B: If creating a user fails, the message is shown as Error: Username already taken — with the "Error:" prefix ( String(createMut.error) ). Other pages (Wrapped, Discover) strip the prefix. Where: web/src/pages/admin/UsersPage.tsx What to do: (A) disable Save while the password field is empty (or don't submit). (B) strip the prefix or use error.message . Acceptance criteria - [ ] Two new tests in UsersPage.test.tsx : Save is disabled / no request for an empty password; the error message is shown without the prefix.
descriptions.github:5684141991: A few actions swallow errors and show nothing, so the user presses a button and nothing seems to happen. Where - web/src/components/PlaylistCard.tsx — Play: catch { // ignore } - web/src/components/home/ContinueListeningSection.tsx — "Jump back in": catch { // ignore … } - web/src/components/StarButton.tsx — silently reverts the star when the request fails What to do: on failure show a short, clear message through useToastStore (e.g. "Couldn't start playback"). Don't change the existing behaviour (optimistic revert etc.). Acceptance criteria - [ ] All three places show a toast on failure. - [ ] Each has a test that makes the API reject and asserts the toast message.
descriptions.github:5684141770: When a library scan can't be started, Admin → Libraries shows the browser's blocking alert() . Everywhere else the app uses the toast for transient messages. Where: web/src/pages/admin/LibrariesPage.tsx (around line 31: alert(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Failed to start scan') ). Toast store: web/src/store/toast.ts — useToastStore.getState().show('message') . Acceptance criteria - [ ] No alert() left; the error appears in the Toast component. - [ ] LibrariesPage.test.tsx is updated: instead of spying on window.alert , assert the message in the toast store.
descriptions.github:5684141489: Follow-up to the player bar issue: other icon-only buttons also rely on title alone. Where (starting points) - web/src/pages/QueuePage.tsx — "Remove" and the drag handle ("Drag to reorder") - web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx — "Create playlist" - web/src/components/DownloadButton.tsx — "Download" / "Remove download" - web/src/components/StarButton.tsx , web/src/components/LyricsPanel.tsx (close button) What to do: add an aria-label (same text as the title ). Acceptance criteria - [ ] The buttons above have an accessible name. - [ ] Existing tests pass; at least two of them get a getByRole('button', { name }) assertion. Feel free to comment here to claim it.
descriptions.github:5684141276: The icon-only buttons in the player bar (Shuffle, Previous, Play/Pause, Next, Repeat, More options, Lyrics, …) only carry a title="…" . title is not a reliable accessible name for screen readers. The whole web app currently has only 5 aria-label s. Where: web/src/components/PlayerBar.tsx (e.g. title="More options" , title="Shuffle" , title="Previous" ). What to do: give every icon-only an aria-label with the same text as its title . For toggle buttons (shuffle/repeat) also add aria-pressed where it makes sense. Acceptance criteria - [ ] Every icon-only button in the player bar has an accessible name. - [ ] Existing tests pass ( npm --workspace web test ) and PlayerBar.test.tsx gets at least one getByRole('button', { name: … }) assertion. See CONTRIBUTING.md for how to set up the project. Feel free to comment here to claim it.

descriptions.github:5683888258: Reproduction On current main , fetch the spec the server serves and look for $ref s that point at schemas it doesn't define: Expected Every $ref in /openapi.json resolves. Actual GET /v1/sessions/{session id}/stream declares its text/event-stream response as $ref: /components/schemas/ServerStreamEvent , but the live document never defines ServerStreamEvent . Only scripts/dump openapi.py adds it, when writing the committed openapi.json , so the checked-in file is fine and the served one isn't. Why it matters /docs and any client generator or validator pointed at a running server's /openapi.json hit an unresolved reference on the session stream, which is the main way clients follow a session. Proposed fix Register the ServerStreamEvent union (and its per-event variants) in the app's OpenAPI document, and have scripts/dump openapi.py reuse that instead of keeping its own copy. The…
descriptions.github:5683879760: Outcome A session can be shared or archived outside Pragma, for example as the base of a pull request description. Current behavior There is no export for a thread. The only way out is copying code blocks one by one. Expected behavior - "Export as Markdown" and "Copy as Markdown" in the session menu. - "Copy as Markdown" on a single message (moved from 396), using the same output format. - Output contains user and assistant messages. descriptions.github:5683511344: Problem or use case There is no omni command that closes or deletes a session. The API supports it ( DELETE /v1/sessions/{id} ), and the web UI can archive. From a terminal, the closest is omni host stop-session . That stops the runner but leaves the session in the list. A script or a user cleaning up test or probe sessions must call the HTTP API by hand, with a bearer token. Proposed solution omni session close ... (archive) and omni session delete ... (with a confirm, or --yes ). Both should take --server and use the same auth as omni session export . Alternatives considered curl -X DELETE with a token from the server's auth flow. It works, but it is undiscoverable and makes users handle tokens themselves. Related: 4834 and 7498 (the agent-side sys session close gaps).

descriptions.github:5682904874: Debugging a live indexing run means grepping stack traces. Structured logs with a correlation id per request make failures traceable end to end. descriptions.github:5681673047: Summary Only SIGQUIT is handled. SIGTERM and SIGINT use the default action, so the process dies at once and leaves the pid file behind. nginx does a fast shutdown on TERM/INT: it closes connections and deletes the pid file. Repro pid logs/r.pid; , start, kill -TERM . - nginx: exits 0, pid file removed. - ruxen: killed by the signal (exit status 143), logs/r.pid left behind. nginx reference src/os/unix/ngx process.c:55-58 (terminate signal); src/os/unix/ngx process cycle.c:660 ( ngx delete pidfile ). Unlocks — Notes Same flag plumbing as SIGQUIT, with no drain. Where in ruxen src/main.rs --- Reproduced on 23a0c43 . Good first issue: small and self-contained. See CONTRIBUTING.md; comment here before starting so two people don't do the same work.
descriptions.github:5681672067: Summary All three directives are ignored, so Set-Cookie from the upstream is passed through unchanged. Repro The upstream sends Set-Cookie: a=b; domain= path=/old/; Secure . Config: proxy cookie domain example.com; proxy cookie path /old/ /new/; proxy cookie flags a httponly samesite=strict nosecure; . - nginx: domain=example.com; path=/new/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict , without Secure . - ruxen: unchanged. nginx reference ngx http proxy module.c:2699 (cookie rewrite), :4564 (flags). Unlocks proxy cookie.t (1–8) and proxy cookie flags.t (1–7, 9–10, 12–14). Both files then pass. Notes It is a response-header rewrite on the proxy path only; supports variables and regex ( / ). It can be split into three PRs, one per directive. Where in ruxen src/config/mod.rs --- Reproduced on 23a0c43 .
descriptions.github:5681671532: Summary proxy method is accepted and ignored, so the upstream always sees the client's method. Repro location /m { proxy method POST; proxy pass } with an upstream that echoes $request method , then curl /m . - nginx: upstream sees POST . - ruxen: upstream sees GET . nginx reference src/http/modules/ngx http proxy module.c:439 (directive), :1236 ( ngx http proxy create request ). Unlocks proxy method.t (2–4; the file then passes). Notes It is a complex value (variables allowed) and inherits from the parent. Render it into the request line in run location handler . Take it off IGNORED STMT in the same PR. Where in ruxen src/config/mod.rs --- Reproduced on 23a0c43 . Good first issue: small and self-contained. See CONTRIBUTING.md; comment here before starting so two people don't do the same work.
descriptions.github:5681671059: Summary types {} is swallowed and default type is ignored. MIME types come from a hardcoded 18-entry table that appends ; charset=utf-8 to text types, and unknown extensions get application/octet-stream . nginx uses the configured types map ( include mime.types in practice), falls back to default type (default text/plain ), and adds no charset unless charset is set. Repro Request /a.foo , /noext and /index.html . - nginx: text/x-foo , text/x-default , text/html . - ruxen: application/octet-stream , application/octet-stream , text/html; charset=utf-8 . nginx reference src/http/ngx http core module.c:311,319 (directives), :3660 (built-in default types), ngx http set content type . Unlocks — Notes Build a per-location HashMap at prepare time; the hot path does one lowercase-extension lookup, as now. Re-measure m3 and static 8k . Keeping the charset suffix would need charset support. Where…
descriptions.github:5681670291: Summary ssl protocols TLSv1 TLSv1.1 TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3; is a hard error ( insecure version rejected: TLSv1 ). That exact line is in common distro default nginx.conf files, so unmodified configs don't load. rustls can't speak TLS 1.0/1.1 anyway. Repro http { ssl protocols TLSv1 TLSv1.1 TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3; ... } , then ruxen -t . - nginx: ok. - ruxen: [emerg] bad value for ssl protocols (insecure version rejected): TLSv1 . nginx reference src/http/modules/ngx http ssl module.c ( ssl protocols bitmask). Unlocks ssl sni reneg.t gets past config load. Its renegotiation subtests then fail by design in rustls, so it won't fully pass. Notes Keep TLSv1.2/1.3 from the list and log [warn] TLSv1, TLSv1.1 are not supported and ignored . A list with only old versions should still be [emerg] . Where in ruxen src/config/mod.rs --- Reproduced on 23a0c43 . Good first issue: small and self-contained. See…

descriptions.github:5681669368: Summary There are three separate reason-phrase tables, and any code they don't list becomes OK : return 413 sends HTTP/1.1 413 OK , and the same goes for 307/308/406/414/416/429/504. 503 says Service Unavailable , where nginx says Service Temporarily Unavailable . nginx sends NNN with an empty reason for codes it doesn't know (205, 418, 599). Repro location = /413 { return 413; } (likewise 307, 504, 418), then curl -si . - nginx: 413 Request Entity Too Large , 307 Temporary Redirect , 504 Gateway Time-out , 418 . - ruxen: 413 OK , 307 OK , 504 OK , 418 OK . - client max body size overflow also answers 413 OK . nginx reference src/http/ngx http header filter module.c:58+ ( ngx http status lines[] ). Unlocks — Notes One const table indexed like nginx's, used by all three call sites. For 418/599, nginx also sends no body and no Content-Type. Where in ruxen src/http.rs , src/file.rs…

descriptions.github:5681659150: What happens writeFd loops until every byte is written, but it returns early, without an error, when write returns 0. The caller sees success while the rest of the frame was dropped. wire.zig treats the same case as an error. Where - tools/zzzbench/tty.zig:39-46 - tools/zzzbench/wire.zig:303-316 ( writeWireBytes returns error.ProbeGone when n == 0 ) Suggested fix Return an error when n == 0 instead of returning normally. A real file descriptor does not return 0 for a non-empty write, so move the loop into a function that takes the write call as a parameter, and test it with a stub that returns 0. tty.zig has no tests today, so register it in tools/zzzbench/tests.zig .

None of them are used. descriptions.github:5681565051: Use case Contributors with multiple saved hive profiles sometimes want to work exclusively on one hive—even when it has no available jobs. For example, I want to keep searching for Bluefin jobs without switching to Kubestellar, while preserving Kubestellar’s URL and registration token. Currently, selecting Bluefin as active doesn’t enforce exclusivity: spread rotates among hives, and ranked falls back when Bluefin has no work. Proposed solution Add per-hive enable/disable controls in just contribute-tui and equivalent CLI commands. Disabled hives should: - Retain their saved URL and token. - Remain visible in the TUI, clearly marked disabled. - Be excluded from new job solicitation under every routing strategy. - Be re-enabled without registration or token rotation. Apply changes to a running relay without restarting it. Allow in-flight work to finish on its original hive. If all hives…
descriptions.github:5681561743: Why The Appearance dialog draws clickable controls, but its keyboard handling currently only supports Escape. Scope Add a visible focus indicator and Tab/Shift+Tab traversal for existing controls. Enter/Space activates the focused action; Escape closes and restores composer focus. Reuse the current appearance actions and limits; this does not depend on a separate disabled-button change. Done when - Theme, text size, UI scale, reading width, Reset, and Done are reachable without a mouse. - Focus remains within the dialog and cannot trigger underlying send/navigation actions. - Values still clamp at existing limits; clicks and keys agree even if all adjustment controls remain present. - Focus is visible in both themes, survives redraw/resize, and never changes the composer draft. Starting points controls, appearance actions, settings keyboard branch.
descriptions.github:5681560876: Why The header/footer show a project basename, which is ambiguous when two folders have the same name and cannot be copied directly. Scope Add a clearly labelled Copy path control next to the header project breadcrumb. Copy the complete current canonical project path using the existing SDL clipboard pattern. Do not change the active folder or add a new global shortcut. Done when - Same-basename projects copy their distinct full paths. - Spaces, Unicode, and long paths copy without the display label's truncation. - During a pending chat switch, copy the project shown by the breadcrumb. - Clipboard failure is reported; clicking does not alter the draft, caret, or chat selection. Starting points displayed project breadcrumb, clipboard pattern.
descriptions.github:5681560437: Why Clearing a library query currently requires editing the text; there is no clear control. Scope Show a clear button inside the query field only when the query is nonempty. Clear via the existing editor/request flow, reset paging, and keep the same scope and modal open. Reuse the existing action/target system. Done when - Clicking clears the query, returns to the first page, and keeps input focus. - A prior in-flight query cannot replace the new empty-query results. - The button never edits the chat draft or activates a selected result. - Empty queries hide the control; IME composition is cancelled cleanly before clearing. Starting points library actions, query field, query drawing.
descriptions.github:5681559956: Why The chat library uses the same No matches status for an empty workspace, empty archives, and a query with no results. Scope Show scope-specific guidance after a completed search. Distinguish an empty query from a nonempty query with no matches. Use existing scope/query/page state; do not add a new search or enrollment path. Done when - Empty Search explains creating/importing a chat; empty Archives explains archiving. - Empty Import Pi explains that there are no importable results in configured Pi storage, without claiming no sessions exist. - A nonempty query says no matches and suggests changing/clearing it. - Searching, indexing, incomplete sources, and errors retain their status rather than being mislabeled as empty. Starting points library scope and status.
descriptions.github:5681559500: Why Text size, scale, and reading width already clamp their values, but their minus/plus buttons still look and behave as enabled at the limits. Scope Render the exhausted direction as disabled and omit its hit target. Keep existing limits: text 12–24 px, UI scale 75–175%, and width 560–1120 px. Reuse the palette and existing adjustment actions. Done when - Each minimum disables only minus; each maximum disables only plus. - Disabled clicks do not change values, enqueue saves, or invalidate layouts. - Moving back into range re-enables the button; Reset restores the normal state. - Disabled controls remain recognizable in dark and light themes. Starting points value clamps, adjustment drawing.
descriptions.github:5681559176: Why The thinking menu supports mouse selection and Escape only; unlike the model picker, arrows and Enter cannot choose a level. Scope Highlight the current thinking level on opening. Up/Down move within Pi's supplied levels, Enter invokes the existing selection action, and Escape cancels. Use Pi's list rather than hardcoded levels. Done when - Keyboard and mouse choose the same level and close the menu. - Arrow movement clamps at the ends; an empty or refreshed list cannot submit a stale index. - Escape does not change the level or composer text. - The highlighted row is visible and distinguishable in both themes. Starting points thinking overlay, existing action, keyboard branch.
descriptions.github:5681558836: Why Shortcuts are implemented and listed in CLI help, but there is no in-app reference. Scope Add a Shortcuts entry in the sidebar opening a read-only help dialog. List existing navigation, sending, stop, search, model, settings, and zoom controls; show Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere. Reuse the appearance dialog's drawing/modal conventions. Done when - Listed shortcuts match the current handlers; no new shortcuts are invented. - Escape/Close restores the previous composer draft, selection, and focus. - Typing while open never edits or sends the draft. - The list is readable at minimum window size, in both themes, and at 75%/175% UI scale. Starting points key dispatch, help text, dialog pattern.
descriptions.github:5681558334: Why The sidebar has wheel scrolling and a virtualized row offset, but no scrollbar showing position or allowing a quick jump. Scope Add a sidebar scrollbar driven by existing row count and sidebar first . Support thumb dragging and track clicks; preserve visible-row virtualization and folder expand/collapse behavior. Done when - With more rows than fit, dragging reaches first/last rows and track clicks move predictably. - No scrollbar appears when all rows fit. - Resize, collapsed folders, and catalog refresh clamp the offset and cancel stale drags safely. - Scrolling does not open/archive a chat or change the selected chat. Starting points row counting and positions, sidebar, existing transcript thumb geometry.
descriptions.github:5681557952: Why The model picker displays six rows at a time and has scrolling/keyboard selection, but no text filtering. Scope Add case-insensitive filtering over Pi's configured model names, IDs, and providers. Reuse the Unicode composer and existing model-selection action; do not introduce another model registry or change provider configuration. Done when - A query finds a configured model by name, ID, or provider; clearing restores the list. - Arrow keys and Enter select the highlighted filtered model, not its old unfiltered index. - Empty/no-match lists cannot select a stale item; Escape restores composer focus and its draft. - Snapshot refresh while filtering preserves identity where possible and safely clears a disappeared selection. Starting points model overlay, selection, query editing pattern.
descriptions.github:5681557551: Why Clipboard copying currently covers the composer/query, not a transcript message. Scope Add a Copy action to user and assistant messages. Copy the original body text, not rendered glyphs, timestamps, reasoning, or tool summaries. Load the selected body off the UI thread rather than decoding the entire conversation. Done when - Unicode, multiline Markdown, and a body larger than 64 KiB copy exactly. - Copying a message leaves the draft, disclosure state, and scroll position unchanged. - Archived/cached messages work; unavailable content and clipboard failure report an error without stale success feedback. - Only the selected message is materialized for the clipboard. Starting points transcript entries/drawing, clipboard pattern.
descriptions.github:5681557164: Why Only the selected chat's header shows runtime state. Sidebar chat rows show titles and availability, not the state of background work. Scope Show a compact labelled status for running/queued work and failures on visible chat rows. Read existing active/parked snapshots; do not launch or poll extra Pi processes. This does not require persistent notifications or unread tracking. Done when - Run work in A, open B, and observe A's status change without reopening A. - Completion removes the running state; failure remains distinguishable until handled. - Indexed and transient parked rows work, including same-titled chats; badges do not steal archive/open hit targets. - Idle UI remains event-driven and only visible rows are drawn. Starting points background snapshots, sidebar drawing.
descriptions.github:5681556782: Why Visited-chat state remains resident. The current measurement script samples a single Linux PID; it does not exercise repeated chat visits or account for the Pi children. Scope Add an isolated Linux benchmark for 100 and 1,000 chats with deterministic histories and drafts. Measure desktop and owned-child memory/CPU separately, navigation latency, idle child count, and residency after revisiting chats. Reuse the existing sampler; do not bundle cache redesign into this issue. Done when - One documented command reproduces both workloads without provider credentials. - Reports distinguish catalog population from actual chat visits and state the history/draft sizes. - Measurements include all owned Pi children and post-idle behavior, not desktop RSS alone. - Missing/departed processes produce explicit incomplete measurements; user sessions are never modified. Starting points baseline…
descriptions.github:5681556447: Why Chat switching retains separate in-memory drafts, but the disk writer persists only the active application's draft. Scope Persist drafts by stable chat identity, including unsent new threads. Reuse the background writer and existing draft/recovery revision rules. Keep source Pi sessions unchanged; an unsent draft must not become a durable workspace member merely because it was saved. Done when - Distinct drafts in chats A and B survive graceful close/restart regardless of which chat was selected. - An unsent new-thread draft survives without enrollment. - A background acknowledgement clears only its accepted revision, not a newer draft or another chat's draft. - Read/write failure is reported without silently discarding the in-memory draft; existing workspace settings remain readable. Starting points parked draft ownership, saveDraft, draft state/writer.
descriptions.github:5681556116: Why Version mismatch and failed verification collapse into PiVersionMismatchOrVerificationFailed . The user cannot tell which version was found or which configured executable failed. Scope Distinguish missing Node, missing Pi entrypoint, incompatible Pi version, and verifier failure/timeout. Show the relevant resolved/configured path, expected and detected versions where available, and the applicable --node / --pi-entry override. Retain strict version checking and ownership of any live verifier. Done when - A missing Node path, missing entrypoint, different Pi version, and hung verifier produce distinct useful diagnostics. - Pi 1.0.0 still reaches Ready. - A failed or timed-out verification neither launches a second runtime nor leaks an owned child. Starting points launch, version verifier, runtime overrides.

descriptions.github:5681551856: 赏金平台 / Platform GitHub 原始链接 / Source URL 漏洞描述 / Description [Bounty $1,000] FP32 ttnn.cumsum returns NaN after infinity or overflow 📝 Background ttnn.cumsum has a regression in its compensated FP32 accumulation path. After the running total becomes +inf or -inf—either because an input contains an infinity or because the sum overflows—subsequent output elements become NaN. This behavior diverges from PyTorch: Input: [1.0, inf, 1.0, 1.0] ttnn: [1.0, inf, nan, nan] torch: [1.0, inf, inf, inf] The regression was introduced by the compensated-summation change in 56811. The compensation calculation performs inf - inf, producing NaN; subsequent scan elements are then poisoned. The issue affects the default FP32 path. The existing disable compensated sum=True path avoids the failure but is deprecated and is not an acceptable long-term workaround. 🎯 What Success Looks Like The bounty is complete…

descriptions.github:5681232376: 🤖 This issue was found and written with AI (Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5). Problem Any fatal error (wrong password, network down, WebUntis maintenance) prints a full Python traceback via logging.exception . That's noisy, especially with --short , where the user expects a tiny output. Proposal - Known errors ( WebUntisError , ValueError from config, Playwright TimeoutError ) → one clear line plus a hint, exit code 1 : - Full traceback only with -v . - Distinct exit codes (e.g. 2 config error, 3 login error, 4 network) so scripts and status bars can react.
descriptions.github:5681232002: 🤖 This issue was found and written with AI (Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5). Problem --clear-session doesn't actually clear the session. In main.py the browser context is created first, and aenter loads storage state.json into it. Only after that does session.clear session() delete the file: The run still uses the old cookies, and aexit writes them back to disk. So the flag is a no-op. Fix - Delete the file before creating the context, e.g. by passing a fresh=True option to BrowserSession or by deleting it in main.py before the async with . - Alternatively, call context.clear cookies() like --form-login does. - Add a test asserting the context is created with storage state=None when --clear-session is given.

descriptions.github:5681087603: Summary codeprism scan . --diff validates the range with SAFE GIT REF RE , which allows a leading - . A value such as --stat , -p or --shortstat is therefore passed to git diff --name-only as an option, and the scan reports "No changed files" and exits 0. In a CI gate, a bad value passes silently instead of failing. (Git rejects branch names starting with - , so this is a hardening gap rather than an easy exploit, but the check exists specifically to keep git arguments safe.) Steps to reproduce Uses a throwaway git repository. Actual behaviour SAFE GIT REF RE = r"^[\w./ ^@{}:+\-]{1,200}$" ( codeprism/cli.py ) matches --stat , -p and --help . Expected behaviour A range starting with - is rejected with the existing "Invalid diff range" message and exit 1. Suggested fix - Require the first character not to be - , for example ^(?!-)[\w./ ^@{}:+\-]{1,200}$ . - Also pass --end-of-options (or…

descriptions.github:5680992241: GroqClient.SystemPrompt hard-codes English: The model handles many languages perfectly well. The only reason the review is English-only is that the prompt says so. What to build The flag should substitute the target language into the prompt and translate the section headings to match, so the output reads naturally rather than as translated English headings over a non-English body. Why it matters This project was built for the developer with no team to ask. That developer is not necessarily an English speaker, and a review you have to translate before you can act on it is a review you will skip. Notes - Default stays English, so nothing changes for existing users. - Accept ISO 639-1 codes ( pt , es , fr , de , ja ) and fall back to English with a warning on stderr for anything unrecognised. - Nothing parses the section names, so they are free to translate.
descriptions.github:5680986143: The CLI reviews local changes ( git diff , --staged , --diff ). It cannot review a pull request that is not checked out locally. What to build GitHub serves the raw diff for any PR at .diff , so this can be a plain HTTP GET followed by the existing review path — no API client, and no authentication needed for public repositories. Why it matters It turns the tool from "review what I am about to commit" into "review what someone sent me", which is the other half of reviewing alone: the maintainer triaging a drive-by contribution with nobody to ask for a second opinion. Notes - Private repositories need a token; treat that as a follow-up, not part of this. - Large PRs will hit the existing 60k-character truncation. That is fine, but the warning should name the PR that was truncated. - Parsing the URL belongs in CliOptions ; fetching belongs in its own small type next to GitDiff .

descriptions.github:5680942128: Problem Sources/MomoApp/Support/KeychainStore.swift:25-39 : setKey first calls SecItemDelete , then return SecItemAdd(...) == errSecSuccess . The method is marked , and every caller ignores the result: - Settings/AI/APIKeySetupView.swift:148 (sets result = .valid right after) - Settings/BrainSettingsView.swift:282 - Settings/ConnectionsSettingsView.swift:125 Scenario The user replaces a working key. SecItemAdd fails (the keychain is locked or access is denied). By then the old key has already been deleted and the new one wasn't saved, yet the UI shows "valid / connected". The next chat fails with an authentication error, far from the real cause. Suggested fix - Update the item with SecItemUpdate , falling back to SecItemAdd , so the old key is never deleted first. - Check the result at each call site (or make setKey throw the OSStatus ) and show an error instead of .valid .
descriptions.github:5680936876: Problem Sources/MomoMCP/MCPClient.swift:56-70 : LineBuffer.append keeps appending data until it sees \n , with no size limit. Both ProcessTransport and UnixSocketTransport use it. The server side already caps its buffer at 16 MB ( MCPSocketServer.swift:191 ); the client side has no cap. Scenario A buggy third-party MCP server streams a huge response, or endless output without a newline. Momo's memory grows until macOS kills the app. Suggested fix - Cap LineBuffer at 16 MB, matching the server. - On overflow, finish the stream with an error and close the transport.
descriptions.github:5680936294: Problem Sources/MomoApp/Context/MCPConnections.swift:66-77 starts the server process with ProcessTransport . If client.connect() throws (for example ClientError.timedOut after the fixed 30 s in MCPClient.swift:149 ) or listTools() throws, the catch block only sets .failed . It never calls client.close() , which is the only path that terminates the process ( MCPClient.swift:49-52 ). clients[id] stays nil , so the next refresh() starts yet another process. Scenario A server configured as npx -y some-server takes more than 30 s to install on first run. Momo marks it failed, but the node process keeps running. Every settings change or refresh adds another orphaned process. Suggested fix - Call await client.close() (or terminate the transport) in the catch . - Make the initialize timeout longer than, or separate from, the per-call timeout.

descriptions.github:5680817038: Contributor problem The test workflow currently runs only on Windows with Python 3.11, although the documentation advertises Python 3.11 or later. Contributors working on storage, categories, analytics, and reports also need a verified way to run those tests from Linux. GIFs have no audio, so leave out the opus flags. Keep Arg::VideoChain(&TRANSCODE CHAIN) so --fps and --resize still work, and register it next to the gif - mp4 line in insert media family . The "looping GIF becomes a single play" warning applies here too. One thing to check: GIFs can have transparent pixels, and VP9 webm can carry alpha ( -pix fmt yuva420p ). If that works, keep it. If not, add a warning saying transparency is lost. Done when conv in.gif out.webm works, the recipe snapshot has the new line, and the pair count at the top of the README is updated. CONTRIBUTING.md has the steps.
