descriptions.github:5680591943: Description cli/mesi-cli.go never closes the HTTP response body. In URL mode the body is fetched at client.Do(req) ( cli/mesi-cli.go:306 ) and read with io.ReadAll(content.Body) ( cli/mesi-cli.go:317 ), but there is no defer content.Body.Close() anywhere, so the http.Response is dropped unread on every path that leaves the URL branch. Impact today is small but real: - the body is read to EOF on the success path, so the connection is handed back to the pool anyway and main returns immediately afterwards; - on every error branch os.Exit(1) is called, and os.Exit runs no deferred functions, so a defer content.Body.Close() placed at the top of the branch would not fire there either — the fds are only reclaimed when the process dies. So no leak is observable from the CLI as it is used today. The defect is the missing Close() itself: it is invisible only because the process is short-lived…

descriptions.github:5680545900: Problem Jenkins users commonly publish JUnit results from a Declarative Pipeline post block. descriptions.github:5680544867: Why this is useful The repository includes a demonstration page, but the CLI only produces Markdown or JSON. descriptions.github:5680544374: Why this is useful Markdown rendering has a dedicated function in core.py, while construction of the JSON envelope currently lives inside cli.main. descriptions.github:5680543864: Why this is useful README and SECURITY explain that failure text is data rather than instructions. That guidance does not travel with a brief when someone copies only the generated Markdown into a coding assistant. An optional short notice inside the brief could make its origin clearer to both the user and the assistant. It would be contextual guidance, not a mechanism that guarantees prevention of prompt injection. Scope Agree on concise wording and placement for an optional data-boundary notice. Do not modify or interpret report instructions, execute commands, or add a hosted-model integration. Acceptance criteria - Use a synthetic failure containing an instruction-like sentence and show the complete proposed output. - State plainly that report contents are untrusted diagnostic data and require independent review. - Count the notice in the character budget, including the…
descriptions.github:5680543331: Why this is useful JSON currently uses two-space indentation, which is pleasant for manual review. In pipelines that immediately parse the result, whitespace adds bytes without adding information. A compact serialization option could reduce artifact size while preserving all records and existing field semantics. It must not be confused with shortening failure content or imposing a total-output budget; those have different effects on what consumers receive. Scope Discuss an explicit JSON-only compact mode using standard-library serialization. Keep pretty-printed JSON as the default unless a separate compatibility decision is made. Acceptance criteria - Confirm that parsing pretty and compact output produces identical data for the same arguments. - Preserve Unicode, escaping, schema version, ordering expectations, and the final newline contract. - Define and test invalid combinations with…
descriptions.github:5680542819: Why this is useful Markdown is useful for sharing briefs, but literal backslash escapes and code fences can be distracting when reading output in a terminal or plain-text log viewer. A dedicated text renderer could serve those users while keeping the same privacy and size guarantees. This should be a small alternative presentation layer, without terminal colors, network calls, or assumptions that the destination supports rich formatting. Scope Propose a plain-text layout for the existing Failure fields and agree whether it shares the Markdown budget option or has a separate clearly named limit. Acceptance criteria - Provide a concrete before/after example containing punctuation-heavy test names and a multiline traceback. - Preserve suite, class, source, kind, message, and details when budget allows. - Keep terminal-control sanitization, secret redaction, deterministic order, and…
descriptions.github:5680542263: Why this is useful The current JSON envelope is convenient for ordinary scripts, but some command-line workflows process one record at a time. JSON Lines could make those integrations simpler without requiring consumers to parse a whole array. This feature would only change serialization: the current parser still reads and validates all inputs before any result is published, and a new format should not accidentally weaken that all-or-error behavior. Scope Discuss a JSONL contract for metadata and failure records, including schema version, empty output, truncation counts, and command-line selection. Acceptance criteria - Define record types and ordering so consumers can identify metadata without guessing from field names. - Keep embedded newlines escaped within one physical line and preserve Unicode and sanitization. - Ensure invalid later input emits no partial success and atomic file…
descriptions.github:5680541611: Why this is useful Scripts comparing briefs across CI runs currently need to reconstruct identity from suite, class, name, kind, message, and details. A documented fingerprint could simplify matching, but careless hashing can create misleading stability or disclose information through guessing attacks. Absolute source paths and excerpt budgets also vary between machines, so simply hashing the serialized output is unlikely to provide a useful contract. Scope Start with a design for an optional fingerprint derived from agreed sanitized identity fields, separate from parser deduplication and without changing its current behavior. Acceptance criteria - Specify normalization, included fields, algorithm, version tag, and handling of source paths. - Explain whether changing a traceback or excerpt budget should change the identifier, with concrete examples. - Do not hash raw secrets or present…
descriptions.github:5680540952: Why this is useful JSON currently reports aggregate counts of truncated messages and details, while each shortened value contains a human-readable omission notice. A consumer that wants to show a truncated badge for one failure must inspect that text, which could also occur literally in a report. Explicit per-field metadata would let integrations distinguish original content from transformation information without parsing an English sentence. Scope Design a backward-compatible extension or new schema version that represents original sanitized length, retained length, and truncation status for message and details. Acceptance criteria - Specify lengths after redaction and explain whether notice characters are included in each count. - Cover untouched, shortened, empty, and literal-notice content without relying on substring detection. - Keep original secret lengths and matched values out…
descriptions.github:5680540423: Why this is useful The CLI emits schema version: 1 and README lists the envelope and Failure fields, but there is no machine-readable schema that downstream scripts can use to validate an output file. A schema describing the existing contract would make integrations easier to build and review. This task documents current behavior; it should not add new fields, rename properties, or invent guarantees about future versions. Scope Add a checked-in JSON Schema for the version 1 envelope and failure records, plus a short pointer from the JSON documentation. Keep runtime dependencies unchanged. Acceptance criteria - Specify required properties, data types, schema version, and the actual supported kind values. - Define whether unknown fields are accepted, explaining the compatibility tradeoff rather than assuming one. - Include representative empty and non-empty valid examples and an…
descriptions.github:5680539876: Why this is useful Many reports put the same short exception text in the message attribute and at the start of the detail body. The current renderer shows both, which can spend a meaningful share of a small context budget on repeated information. A conservative presentation rule could improve readability, but fuzzy similarity or broad prefix deletion might remove an important distinction in an assertion. Scope Evaluate an opt-in Markdown-only rule for exact duplicated message lines after sanitization. Preserve the original structured fields and avoid changing parser deduplication. Acceptance criteria - Provide synthetic examples for an exact first-line duplicate, a near match, and a genuinely repeated diagnostic line. - Define treatment of whitespace and omission notices; do not accidentally compare truncated text as full evidence. - Keep differing messages and details intact and…
descriptions.github:5680539332: Why this is useful The Markdown header currently reports one total for all unique failure records. With many suites, a reader must scan the individual blocks to understand where failures cluster. A small per-suite summary could help prioritize investigation, particularly when the output budget omits later details. It must clearly summarize extracted unique records rather than claiming to reproduce original runner counters or the total number of executed tests. Scope Discuss an optional summary grouped by the suite identity already available in Failure. Do not change parsing, suite ancestry, deduplication, or failure selection. Acceptance criteria - Include a synthetic report with repeated suite names across reports and define the grouping key explicitly. - Ensure totals agree with the complete extracted failure set, including records whose details are omitted. - Bound summary size and…
descriptions.github:5680538872: Why this is useful The renderer deliberately keeps an ordered prefix of complete failure blocks. If the first block is too large, a brief may contain only the total and an omission notice even when later failures have useful short descriptions. Some workflows would benefit from seeing every selected test identity before allocating remaining space to details. This would be an alternative presentation strategy, not a parser-order change or a new failure filter. Scope Prototype an opt-in summary-first renderer that budgets concise identities before adding detailed blocks. Keep the current ordered-prefix strategy available. Acceptance criteria - Compare both strategies on a synthetic report with one large failure followed by several small failures. - Specify deterministic allocation and tie-breaking without implying all failure details were retained. - Count every summary, heading, and…
descriptions.github:5680538142: Why this is useful Character slicing uses Python code points, which is the documented budget unit, but a visible character can contain several code points. An excerpt boundary can separate an accent from its letter or split a joined emoji in a test message. This is mainly a readability issue and does not justify changing the tool into a tokenizer or silently adopting a new budget unit. Scope Evaluate conservative display-boundary adjustments for combining marks and joined sequences while keeping the current Unicode-character budget contract explicit. Discuss dependency costs before choosing an algorithm. Acceptance criteria - Use small synthetic cases with combining accents, variation selectors, and joined emoji around both excerpt boundaries. - Never exceed the agreed retained-content limit after adjusting a boundary; explain any under-filled budget. - Keep ordinary ASCII excerpt…
descriptions.github:5680537467: Why this is useful The existing excerpt function keeps a character-counted prefix and suffix, preserving the final exception in long traces. It can nevertheless cut through the middle of a filename, source line, or exception sentence. A line-aware option could make the retained evidence easier to read while retaining the bounded output goal. Exact character slicing remains a reasonable default and is covered by existing tests. Scope Design an optional excerpt strategy that favors complete lines near the head and tail, with a defined fallback for one extremely long line. Acceptance criteria - Compare current and proposed output on a synthetic multiline traceback with a terminal exception. - Define the retained-character budget, marker overhead, and exact omitted-character or omitted-line accounting. - Keep useful content from both ends without duplicating overlapping lines or producing…
descriptions.github:5680536950: Why this is useful The CLI excerpts failure messages and details, but suite, class, test name, and source fields can still be very long. Because Markdown currently includes only complete failure blocks, a large parameterized test name can consume the budget and prevent even a short assertion from appearing. The existing output behavior is documented, so a new display policy should be optional or explicitly reviewed rather than silently changing the contract. Scope Define per-field display limits for Markdown metadata with visible omission markers. Preserve complete structured values in JSON unless a separately agreed policy says otherwise. Acceptance criteria - Use a synthetic parameterized test name and long class/source fields that currently hide a useful short failure. - Keep secret removal before display clipping and avoid cutting generated redaction markers. - Count escaping and…
descriptions.github:5680536433: Why this is useful Sanitization occurs before excerpt , which correctly avoids exposing the raw matched value. However, the excerpt slices arbitrary character positions. A short detail budget applied to TOKEN=[REDACTED] can retain only pieces of the replacement marker around the omission notice. That does not reveal the original secret, but it makes the resulting text look corrupted and obscures whether content was hidden for privacy or shortened for length. Scope Make excerpting treat the generated redaction marker as an indivisible display token while keeping retained-content budgets and omission notices clearly defined. Acceptance criteria - Add a synthetic reproduction with the boundary inside [REDACTED] at both the head and tail. - Specify behavior when the marker is longer than the requested retained-character budget. - Never recover or reintroduce original text to fill an excerpt…
descriptions.github:5680535902: Why this is useful The control sanitizer already removes bidirectional embedding and isolate controls. Its explicit ranges do not include every Unicode directional mark, such as U+061C, U+200E, and U+200F. These marks can affect how mixed-direction failure text appears, but they also have legitimate uses in Arabic and Hebrew text. Expanding deletion without examples would trade one readability problem for another. Scope Create a focused design for these three directional marks: preserve, remove, or visibly annotate them under a documented policy. Do not strip all non-ASCII text. Acceptance criteria - Use synthetic mixed-direction test names and traces, including legitimate Arabic or Hebrew text. - Show the visual or copied-text problem motivating any change and specify default versus opt-in behavior. - Preserve ordinary Unicode content and all existing terminal-control and newline…
descriptions.github:5680535390: Why this is useful A reader currently sees replacement markers but cannot distinguish how many recognized matches were removed, or which broad rule families were involved. Optional summary counts could make it easier to review an output transformation and detect unexpected over-redaction. Such counts must not be presented as proof that the brief is safe: zero matches only means that no supported pattern matched the available fields. Scope Discuss aggregate redaction statistics by a small stable set of categories. Keep raw matched strings, secret lengths, and matching context out of both output and diagnostics. Acceptance criteria - Define whether overlapping patterns count once and how repeated sanitization avoids inflating totals. - Use synthetic fixtures showing zero matches, repeated values, overlapping rules, and multiple failure fields. - Keep metadata optional or versioned and…
descriptions.github:5680534881: Why this is useful Failure traces and report paths can reveal a developer username through paths such as /home/demo-person/project/test.py or C:\Users\DemoPerson\project\test.py . These are not credentials and are intentionally outside the current generic secret patterns. Some users still need to remove that personal context before sharing a brief, while keeping relative project paths useful for debugging. This is separate from normalizing report source paths. Scope Design an explicit privacy option that masks configured home-directory prefixes in every visible failure field, without discovering arbitrary personal files or rewriting paths by default. Acceptance criteria - Cover synthetic POSIX and Windows prefixes, separators, case policy, and paths containing spaces. - Use path-boundary-aware replacement so a short prefix cannot corrupt unrelated filenames or prose. - Preserve enough…
descriptions.github:5680534411: Why this is useful A failure may contain a JSON fragment represented as escaped text, such as {\"password\":\"demo-value\"} where the backslashes are literal characters in the displayed diagnostic. The current redactor operates on the displayed text; it is not an arbitrary decoder. Recursively decoding every field would risk changing useful evidence and creating unpredictable runtime costs. Contributors could first define whether one layer of JSON string escaping warrants support; ordinary unescaped JSON assignments are already handled by the current matcher. Scope Focus on one layer of JSON string escaping around a secret assignment. Demonstrate a synthetic missed pattern and design a single bounded normalization or matching step. Do not add recursive decoding, base64 decoding, or URL handling; URL query values belong to the separate query-redaction proposal. Acceptance criteria…
descriptions.github:5680533963: Why this is useful The assignment matcher accepts identifier names containing words such as TOKEN or SECRET anywhere in the key. Harmless diagnostics such as token count=17 or secret length=12 are therefore candidates for masking even when the numbers explain the failing assertion. Relaxing this behavior blindly could expose real credentials, so the useful contribution is a small policy change supported by both sensitive and harmless synthetic examples. Scope Discuss a conservative key-boundary or narrow exception policy. Target diagnostic counters rather than introducing a general disable-redaction switch. Acceptance criteria - Provide before/after examples showing the lost debugging information and the intended supported exception. - Include credential names with prefixes, suffixes, hyphens, quotes, and varied case as negative controls. - Keep genuine credential assignments masked and…
descriptions.github:5680533430: Why this is useful A project-specific account number, internal host, or invented credential may not match any built-in heuristic. Users currently cannot supply exact values they already know should disappear. An explicitly selected local literal list could complement the heuristics without adding a regex language or sending report content to another service. This should remain optional because treating broad strings as secrets can destroy useful diagnostic context. Scope Design a small literal-redaction input contract, including encoding, maximum file size, minimum entry length, ordering, and error behavior. Do not scan the environment or home directory automatically. Acceptance criteria - Agree on a CLI interface and ensure no file is read unless the user selects it. - Use bounded literal matching and define overlapping, duplicate, blank, and Unicode entry behavior. - Ensure errors…
descriptions.github:5680532921: Why this is useful Provider prefixes and assignment patterns do not cover a private key represented as a multiline PEM block in failure details. descriptions.github:5680523418: Feature Factory Simulation & Abstraction What to Solve? Binary Factorium must run on extremely limited hardware ( ), and thus cannot naively use a tiled simulation or the conventional model. The constrains together make it hard to solve easily. What should the simulator essentially contain or do ideally? It should: - Update O(1) when nothing changes - Update O(n) or O(log(n)) when changes happen (with n = parts to update ) - Not hang when numerous updates happen in a short period of time (also in long periods ideally) - Consume a fixed amount of RAM at any point. - Possibly be asynchronous. - Be Binary-Spectacular ;) I am not an expert in this field ;-; (\ unlike what most factory games with large/infinite world target, Binary Factorium's primary targets are the Fri3d Badges)

descriptions.github:5679932145: The cheapest entry left in the ratchet. Array.prototype.sort() sorts in place , so it mutates the array it was given; toSorted() returns a new one. Why this one is worth doing properly rather than mechanically Two of the three production call sites are in data-table.component.ts , which sorts rows it was handed through an input() . Sorting those in place mutates the caller's array — a signal's value, in most cases — which is how a table can reorder data a parent component still believes it owns, without the parent's signal ever being set. Swapping to toSorted() is the fix, but each site is worth a glance to see whether anything downstream was relying on the mutation. Note toSorted() needs a reasonably current runtime target; it is available in the browsers this project targets and in the Node used for specs. descriptions.github:5678907905: 📝 Background ttnn.cumsum has a regression in its compensated FP32 accumulation path. After the running total becomes +inf or -inf—either because an input contains an infinity or because the sum overflows—subsequent output elements become NaN. This behavior diverges from PyTorch: Input: [1.0, inf, 1.0, 1.0] ttnn: [1.0, inf, nan, nan] torch: [1.0, inf, inf, inf] The regression was introduced by the compensated-summation change in 56811. The compensation calculation performs inf - inf, producing NaN; subsequent scan elements are then poisoned. The issue affects the default FP32 path. The existing disable compensated sum=True path avoids the failure but is deprecated and is not an acceptable long-term workaround. 🎯 What Success Looks Like The bounty is complete when all of the following are satisfied: - FP32 ttnn.cumsum preserves IEEE/PyTorch behavior after +inf . - FP32 ttnn.cumsum…

descriptions.github:5677602459: cmd dmesg is a stub. Kernel logs go to serial (and the boot framebuffer early on) but there is no buffer userspace can read back, or if there is one it is not wired to a syscall. First step is checking what DEBUG in src/kernel/debug.h actually emits and whether a ring buffer exists. If not, add a small one behind the existing log path, then an extended syscall that snapshots it out under a lock, then make dmesg print it. Worth deciding what release builds do since most logging is debug only.
descriptions.github:5677600372: cmd lspci in src/usr/shell/shell cmds.cpp prints a stub line. PCI enumeration happens at boot in src/drivers/bus/pci/ but userspace never sees the device list. Needs a new extended syscall (297 or wherever the numbering is by then) that fills an array of small descriptors (bus, slot, function, vendor id, device id, class code) and returns the total count, same shape as SYS INPUT ENUM DEVICES. Then the builtin just prints the table. include/uapi/input.h plus the input enum case in src/kernel/core/syscall.cpp are the reference for the uapi side.
descriptions.github:5677599797: There is no netstat. The TCP and UDP tables live in src/net/tcp.cpp and src/net/udp.cpp but nothing exports counts to userspace (sockets in use, per state, rx/tx bytes). Simplest version is a small extended syscall filling a struct with tcp and udp socket counts per state, next free number is 297. sys net status in src/net/net.cpp is the pattern to copy, and the input enum devices case in src/kernel/core/syscall.cpp shows the array-plus-count shape. Then a netstat builtin in src/usr/shell/shell cmds.cpp that prints it. The socket tables are plain arrays so ktesting the counters is easy.
descriptions.github:5677599522: Every UDP socket has one 1500 byte receive slot with overwrite semantics (src/net/udp.cpp). If two datagrams land before the app calls recvfrom the first one is gone, and nothing reports it either. Turning the slot into a small ring, 4 entries or so, would fix the common case. The receive handoff runs inside net poll() under the table spinlock so the write path has to stay cheap, a memcpy into a preallocated ring is fine. Some way to see overflow would be good too, a debug warn or a dropped counter.
descriptions.github:5677599224: Every resolve goes out on the wire even when we just resolved the same name. dns resolve() in src/net/dns.cpp already retries three times with fresh transaction ids, there is just no cache anywhere. A small table of the last few answers with a short TTL (30-60 seconds is plenty for this stack) would do. The resolver runs from syscall context so keep it under the existing locks. A ktest for expiry and eviction can go next to the dns tests in src/net/dns tests.cpp.

descriptions.github:5677370394: Problem you're trying to solve The OpenSSF Scorecard check "Pinned-Dependencies" reports three unpinned NuGet restores: the dotnet restore in Dockerfile , and the restores in .github/workflows/build.yml and publish.yml . descriptions.github:5677195369: positionAgainstRange in src/utils/version.ts throws instead of returning a value when any version component exceeds Number.MAX SAFE INTEGER . This is live on main today. The boundary is exact: positionAgainstRange(" ", " ") returns "satisfies" , and throws TypeError: Invalid major version . Fifteen digits are fine, sixteen or more throw. It throws for every range, including . Why it throws semver.satisfies routes through Range.test() , which wraps new SemVer(version) in a try/catch and returns false . semver.ltr and semver.gtr route through outside() , which constructs new SemVer(version, options) with no guard. positionAgainstRange calls all three, so the unguarded pair is what throws. Why it is reachable looksLikeVersion admits unbounded digits, so nothing upstream filters these out. A dependency whose own package.json under node modules carries a nanosecond-epoch version, the shape a…

descriptions.github:5676783179: Description Follow-up from 64 / PR 255 (review finding). src/BinaryDownloader.php ( download() , the curl setopt array() call): the return value is ignored. If cURL rejects one option, the remaining ones are skipped silently, so the HTTPS-only and redirect limits could be missing without any error. Also curlOptions() is protected static and called with static:: , so a subclass can override the security settings. Where to start Throw DownloadException::downloadFailed($url, ...) when curl setopt array() returns false; call self::curlOptions() or make it private. descriptions.github:5676728882: Why Some searches expand a tree of decisions one ply at a time: a game, a plan, a sequence of tool calls. The full tree does not fit, and there is no stored graph. Monte Carlo tree search keeps the branches it has tried, picks the next one with an upper confidence bound, and backs a score up the path. 133 covers finding a path through a successor function. This issue is the tree of sampled decisions on top of that idea. Proposed API In a new package search : Options: - WithIterations(n int) , default 100. - WithExploration(c float64) , default math.Sqrt2 . This is the UCB1 constant. - WithRand(r rand.Rand) . When nil, each rollout picks a uniform legal action with crypto/rand . A non-nil source makes the search reproducible. descriptions.github:5676728489: Why Nearest-neighbor search for retrieval keeps a stack of graphs. The top layer is sparse. The bottom layer contains every point. A search starts at the top, greedily walks to a closer neighbor, then drops a layer. That is the HNSW search. The points stay in the caller's table. The graph stores ids, because a vector is not a comparable label in any useful way. This issue is the layered graph and the greedy search. It is not a database. There is no index file, no metadata filter, and no delete. Proposed API A new package nn : Behavior - distance must be zero or positive. A negative distance returns an error at search or insert time. - m and efConstruction below 1 return an error from New . A nil distance returns an error. - k or ef below 1 returns an error from Search . - Insert of an id that is already present does nothing and returns nil. - The neighbor sets are chosen by the HNSW…

descriptions.github:5676728025: Why A block DAG is not a chain. One way to order it is to paint a well-connected subset blue and leave the rest red. A set is a k-cluster when every member has at most k other members that it cannot reach and that cannot reach it. The largest such set is expensive to find. The greedy coloring used by GHOSTDAG walks in topological order and adds a vertex to the blue set when the blue anticone is still within k. This is that coloring. It is not a node, and it does not choose a block for a peer to mine on. HeaviestBranch is the walk on a tree. This is the coloring on a DAG. Proposed API In dag : Behavior - Directed acyclic graphs only. Otherwise gograph.ErrNotDirected or gograph.ErrDAGHasCycle . - k below 0 returns dag.ErrInvalidK . - Two vertices are incomparable when neither can reach the other. - The walk order is the stable topological order, the same one TopologySort returns. - A…

An author outside the expected set still counts as one distinct author, which can only make the count…
descriptions.github:5676727518: Why Fork choice on a tree of blocks walks from the root and, at each block, follows the child whose subtree carries the most weight. GHOST and LMD-GHOST are that walk. The weight is whatever the caller counts: work, stake, or the latest vote of each validator. The library does not know which. Proposed API In dag : Behavior - Directed graphs only. Otherwise gograph.ErrNotDirected . - A vertex with two incoming edges, or a vertex not reachable from root, returns dag.ErrNotTree . - A cycle returns gograph.ErrDAGHasCycle . - Subtree weight is the vertex's own weight plus the subtree weights of its children. A vertex is not counted twice. - Ties break by GetAllVertices order of the children. - The returned path starts at root and ends at a leaf. Vertices are the graph's own pointers. - Negative weights are allowed. They only change which child wins. - Missing root…

Proposed API In flow , beside MaxFlow : Successive shortest paths with potentials. Costs may be negative. A negative cycle in the residual graph returns flow.ErrNegativeCycle . An undirected edge shares its capacity across the two directions, and that capacity is not doubled. - For every vertex other than source and sink, flow in equals flow out. - Flow on an edge stays inside its capacity. - Among shipments of…

descriptions.github:5676726745: Why Some DAGs are ordered by a score that includes the ancestors, not by the vertex alone. A transaction pool ranks a transaction by the total fee of itself and everything that must come before it, divided by the total size of that same set. StableTopologySort can compare vertices, and it cannot see that sum. Proposed API In dag : Behavior - Directed acyclic graphs only. Otherwise gograph.ErrNotDirected or gograph.ErrDAGHasCycle . - The set for a vertex is itself plus every vertex that can reach it. - The key is the sum of num over that set, divided by the sum of den over that set. - A denominator sum of 0 returns dag.ErrZeroDenominator . - Ties break by GetAllVertices order. - Returned vertices are the graph's own pointers, one per vertex in the graph. - Empty graph: nil, nil. - This is a ranking, not a topological order. A later vertex can rank ahead of an ancestor. Callers who need a…
descriptions.github:5676726508: Why Callers often need the best few items, not a full ordering. A mempool keeps the highest-paying transactions. A ranking keeps the top vertices by score. Retrieval keeps the nearest matches. A full sort does more work than that, and it allocates a second copy of the whole list. Proposed API In util : Behavior - k below 0 returns util.ErrInvalidK . k of 0 returns an empty slice and a nil error. - A nil better returns an error. - A nil or empty items returns an empty slice. - The result is a new slice. items is left as it was. - Equal items keep their original order. - Running time is linear in the length of items times log of k , using a heap of size k . The doc comment says so. A caller who wants a nucleus-style prefix computes it from this ordered prefix. The function does not grow a sampling API. Tests - Ten integers, k of 3, the three largest in order. - Ties: two equal best items…
descriptions.github:5676726283: Why AStar ( 185) keeps every unsettled vertex in a heap. When the frontier is large, the memory is the problem. Iterative deepening A repeats a depth-first search with a rising limit on the estimated total cost, and stores only the current path. Planners use it when the graph of states does not fit in memory. Proposed API In path , with the same cost and heuristic contract as AStar : Behavior - Costs must be zero or positive. A negative cost returns path.ErrNegativeWeight . - The search raises the limit to the smallest f-value that was beyond the previous limit. - It returns a cheapest path when the heuristic is admissible. The doc comment says so. It does not check the heuristic. - Missing vertices, an unreachable goal, and start equal to goal follow AStar . - Ties break by vertex and edge order. - The doc comment says AStar is the better choice when the frontier fits in memory…
descriptions.github:5676725921: Why On a graph that branches widely, keeping every partial path is too expensive. Beam search keeps a fixed number of them and drops the rest. Decoders use it to keep a few partial sequences. The same bound keeps a path search inside a memory limit. The result can miss the cheapest path. That is the trade. Proposed API In path : Behavior - width below 1 returns path.ErrInvalidWidth . - Partial paths are simple. A vertex is not repeated on one path. - At each step the search keeps the width partial paths with the best score. Ties break by vertex order. - If the goal is never among the kept paths, path.ErrUnreachable . - Missing start or goal: gograph.ErrVertexDoesNotExist . - start equals goal: a one-vertex path and cost 0, for any positive width. - Returned vertices are the graph's own pointers. - The same graph, width, and score give the same path on every run. - The doc comment says a…
descriptions.github:5676725632: Why A route from one vertex to one other vertex does not need a distance for every vertex. Searching forward from the start and backward from the goal meets in the middle and settles fewer vertices on a large graph. Payment-channel routing and road routing both do this. Proposed API In path , beside AStar ( 185): Behavior - Directed graphs: the backward search walks incoming edges. Every later layout pass throws a NullReferenceException from EventManager.RaiseEffectiveViewportChangedEvents , so new content never gets Loaded and the window stops updating. descriptions.github:5673427734: Current behavior 🐛 BorderVisual (Skia) replaces its RectangleClip objects whenever the border or corner radius geometry changes, but never disposes the old ones. In UpdatePathsAndCornerClip() , the old childClipCausedByCornerRadius and backgroundClip are just set to null and new clips are created (L203-L212, L330-L346). Since 24230, RectangleClip caches one geometry (a native SKPath ) and only releases it in DisposeInternal() (RectangleClip.skia.cs L42). Nothing calls Dispose() on a replaced clip, so its cached path is freed only by the SKPath finalizer when the GC gets around to it, not deterministically. Impact is low: it is bounded to one path per replaced clip and the finalizer does clean it up eventually. It can only pile up between GCs, for example while a rounded Border is being resized or animated frame after frame. This was confirmed by code inspection on master (7a2214115d5)…

descriptions.github:5670511660: docs/CONTRIBUTING.md tells contributors to run three commands before pushing: ruff check, ruff format --check, and pytest. The CI check job also runs mypy over taken/, which the contributor list omits. A contributor following the doc would be surprised by a CI failure they could have caught locally. Evidence: - docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:41 - .github/workflows/ci.yml Expected behavior: Add mypy to the pre-push command list in docs/CONTRIBUTING.md. Why it matters: A contributor following the doc gets a surprise CI failure they could have caught locally. The doc should match the pipeline. Found during an automated audit of the codebase.
descriptions.github:5670510748: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/CONTRIBUTING.md both describe the vendored-console-copy rule and give a re-copy command, but both only mention checks.py and verdict.py. The CI docs-sync job checks three pairs, including taken/budget.py vs docs/console/py/budget.py. A contributor editing taken/budget.py who follows only the docs would not re-copy it, and only CI would catch the drift. Evidence: - docs/ARCHITECTURE.md - docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:47 - .github/workflows/ci.yml Expected behavior: Update the re-copy commands in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/CONTRIBUTING.md to include taken/budget.py, matching the three pairs CI actually checks. Why it matters: A contributor who follows only the docs would drift the vendored copy and learn about it from a red CI run instead of the docs. Found during an automated audit of the codebase.
descriptions.github:5670510245: The Modules section of docs/ARCHITECTURE.md lists cli.py, checks.py, verdict.py, graphql.py, discover.py, and mcp server.py, but omits taken/budget.py (API budget tiers, worker sizing) and taken/health.py (the --health maintainer report). descriptions.github:5670508013: In run gql attempt, when the gh subprocess exits nonzero and stderr is empty, the raised error is ' gh api graphql failed: ' with nothing after the colon. The user gets no actionable detail about what failed. Expected: fall back to the return code or stdout content when stderr is empty, so the message always names the failure. Evidence: - taken/graphql.py:227 - taken/graphql.py:252 Expected behavior: Fall back to the return code or stdout content when stderr is empty, so the raised error always names the failure. Why it matters: An error message that ends at the colon is a dead end for anyone debugging at 2am. Found during an automated audit of the codebase.
descriptions.github:5670507157: The --limit help text says 'max open issues to check per owner/repo scan target', which is true for scan mode. But --discover passes args.limit into DiscoverOptions(limit=...), where limit means max candidates returned, a different semantic. The MCP discover candidates tool documents the correct semantic ('Max candidates to return'). Expected: the CLI help should name both semantics, or the discover path should get its own flag wording. A user tuning --discover --limit 5 expecting 5 issues per repo instead gets at most 5 candidates total. Evidence: - taken/cli.py:74 - taken/cli.py:483 Expected behavior: Name both semantics in the --limit help text, or give the discover path its own flag wording. Why it matters: A user tuning --discover --limit 5 expecting five issues per repo gets five candidates total. That is a usability trap sitting in the flagship mode. Found during an automated…
descriptions.github:5670506268: --jobs is validated (--jobs must be at least 1, exit 3), and the decay-day flags use non negative int, but --limit and --min-contributors use plain type=int: --limit -5 silently scans zero issues and exits 0 with a 'no open issues found' note, and --min-contributors -3 is silently meaningless. --explore-floor takes any float even though it is a probability (default 0.15). The same gap exists on the MCP side: discover candidates accepts negative pr idle days / claim silence days / claim silence complex days with no validation, and scan repo(limit=-5) returns an all-zero summary indistinguishable from a genuinely empty repo. Expected: the same non-negative (and range) validation the codebase already applies to the other numeric inputs. Evidence: - taken/cli.py:74 - taken/cli.py:98 - taken/cli.py:126 - taken/cli.py:50 - taken/mcp server.py:157 - taken/mcp server.py:252 Expected behavior…
descriptions.github:5670505846: Unparseable targets go through parse error, which deliberately returns exit code 3 (the code comments that a usage error must exit 3 without touching the network). But --discover given targets and --health given bad targets go through argparse parser.error, which exits 2. Scripts or agents that distinguish exit 3 as the usage-error contract get mixed signals depending on which flag was misused. Expected: one consistent exit code for all usage errors. This is low impact since both codes are nonzero, but the codebase states its own contract and then violates it in two paths. Evidence: - taken/cli.py:41 - taken/cli.py:372 - taken/cli.py:378 - taken/cli.py:380 Expected behavior: Use one consistent usage-error exit code across all CLI paths, matching the documented contract of 3 from the parse error comment. Why it matters: Scripts and agents key off exit codes, including our own scout…
descriptions.github:5670504865: The scan issue claims docstring describes a claim as waiting when it is older than claim wait days, but waiting entry and quiet entry return entries when age days == wait days (they only reject age days < wait days). The inclusive boundary is arguably the better behavior, but the docstring and code disagree by one day; pick one and make both match. Evidence: - taken/health.py:212 - taken/health.py:178 - taken/health.py:196 Expected behavior: Pick one boundary and make the docstring match the code. The inclusive code behavior looks like the right one to keep. Why it matters: One-day disagreements between docs and code are exactly how the next contributor introduces a real off-by-one. Found during an automated audit of the codebase.
descriptions.github:5670503339: truncated is computed as len(issues) = options.issue limit, so a repo with exactly issue limit open issues and nothing more is flagged as truncated even though the listing is complete. The flag should only be set when there is evidence of more data, for example when a full final page was returned. Minor, but it can send a maintainer looking for issues that do not exist. Evidence: - taken/health.py:349 Expected behavior: Set truncated only when there is evidence of more data, for example a full final page, instead of the = comparison against issue limit. Why it matters: A false truncated flag sends a maintainer hunting for issues that do not exist. Found during an automated audit of the codebase.
descriptions.github:5670501677: pace search is defined but never called anywhere in the audited files; the live pacing path is wait search pace called from gh api run while holding search lock. Dead code carrying a docstring that describes live behavior risks a future reader wiring it in (which would double-pace searches) or relying on behavior that is never exercised. It should be removed or covered by a test that pins the intended pacing contract. Evidence: - taken/checks.py:437 Expected behavior: Remove the dead helper, or pin it with a test if it is meant to be the future pacing contract. It should not sit there looking live while nothing calls it. Why it matters: Dead code with a live-sounding docstring misleads the next reader into wiring it in, which would double-pace searches. Keep the codebase honest. Found during an automated audit of the codebase.

descriptions.github:5670344064: Problem yaatv currently emits its low-bitrate source warning whenever the detected bitrate is below the configured threshold. That warning is useful for lossy sources such as MP3 or AAC, but it can be misleading for lossless formats such as FLAC, ALAC, WAV, or AIFF. A lossless source can have a comparatively low bitrate because of its content or compression efficiency without representing degraded source quality. Requested behavior Only emit the low-bitrate source-quality warning when the source codec/format is one where bitrate is a meaningful quality signal. The change should: - preserve the existing warning for applicable lossy sources; - avoid the warning for clearly lossless sources such as FLAC, ALAC, WAV, and AIFF; - keep the existing warning threshold unchanged; - add focused unit tests for both lossy and lossless cases; - preserve --no-warn behavior. Current workaround Users of…

descriptions.github:5670236246: Problem When yaatv generates the default output filename, it reads artist/title metadata from the audio file. The current artist lookup recognizes values such as artist , albumartist , ID3 TPE1 , and MP4 ©ART , but some supported containers expose equivalent artist metadata under other common keys. In particular: - MP4/M4A can use aART for album artist; - ASF/WMA commonly uses Author . When those are the only populated artist fields, yaatv can fall back to the source filename instead of producing the expected Artist - Title.mp4 default name. Requested behavior Extend artist metadata lookup so the default output-name path also recognizes the relevant MP4 and ASF/WMA artist aliases. At minimum: - recognize MP4 aART ; - recognize ASF/WMA Author ; - preserve the current precedence for existing artist fields; - keep title handling unchanged unless a format-specific test shows a corresponding…

descriptions.github:5670139562: Description Describe the bug There is a responsiveness issue in the CaseStudyBanner component. On medium to smaller screen sizes (before the 600px breakpoint where the layout stacks vertically), the absolute-positioned "CASE STUDY" ribbon in the top right overlaps with the banner text ("Discover how HPE uses Meshery to manage SPIRE"). This overlapping text makes the banner difficult to read and hurts the user experience. Expected Behavior The banner text should have sufficient padding or margins on the right side so that it clears the "CASE STUDY" ribbon without any overlapping, regardless of the screen width. Screenshots Steps to Reproduce 1. Navigate to a page that contains the Case Study Banner. 2. Slowly resize the browser window from a large desktop view down to a medium width (around 600px - 1000px). 3. Observe that the "CASE STUDY" ribbon on the top-right overlaps with the…
descriptions.github:5670088931: Context AudioStoreDataSource reads one ARTIST string per song from MediaStore, but real-world tags look like "Shakira feat. Bizarrap" or "A, B & C" — one row per song can never answer "show me every song by B". There is even a TODO about this in AudioStoreDataSource.kt:82-87 . The web version already solved the parsing ( origin/legacy:src/lib/stores/artist.svelte.ts ); the native app should port that semantics into real tables instead of re-deriving it in memory. Port exactly this behavior: What to do - PR1 — schema + sync: artists(id auto, name, normalizedName UNIQUE, coverUri?) + song artists(songId, artistId) junction. Parse during the library sync inside a Room transaction on Dispatchers.IO . Note: only the primary artist has a MediaStore ARTIST ID — collaborators get synthetic ids keyed by normalized name, so design for that from the start. - PR2 — wire the artists screen to the…
descriptions.github:5670086592: Context The web version ( legacy branch) exported playlists to a JSON backup copied to the clipboard, and could import it back ( origin/legacy:src/lib/db/backup.ts ). Users migrating to the native app would love their playlists to travel with them — and the format is fully documented in the old code, so no guesswork is needed. The legacy format: - songIds are MediaStore ids stored as text (see origin/legacy:src/lib/db/db/schema.ts : song id TEXT ). - Import matched playlists by name , skipped already-present songs, and mapped name == "favoritos" && id == 1 to favorites. What to do - Single PR: "import backup" entry point (paste-from-clipboard, mirroring the legacy UX) that parses the JSON above, validates formatVersion , and matches each songId against the current device MediaStore library. - Songs not found on this device must be reported, not silently dropped (e.g. "3 of 42 songs not…
descriptions.github:5670084875: Context Playlists today are List(10) placeholders in features/playlists/presentation/playlists.kt : the empty state is unreachable, both FABs are dead ( onClick = {} ), and there is no persistence at all. Room is half-declared — room-ktx is in app/build.gradle.kts but room-compiler is absent, so zero / can compile. The favorites design decision lives separately in 16 (read it first: kind column, not the "favoritos" sentinel). The legacy schema ( origin/legacy:src/lib/db/db/schema.ts ) is the porting reference: playlists(id, name, date created) + playlists songs(id, playlist id FK cascade, song id TEXT) — note song id is text (MediaStore id as string) and the old table lacked a uniqueness constraint, which once forced a duplicate cleanup. What to do - PR1 — Room setup done right: add room-compiler + KSP config in the same commit as the entities (compiler alone or entities alone means…
descriptions.github:5670083422: Context The web version ( legacy branch) stored favorites as a playlist literally named "favoritos" (id 1). The native app inherited the hack: playlists.kt hardcodes a "favoritos" sentinel row. If the user renames that playlist, favorites silently "disappear", and any playlist the user names favoritos collides with it. What to do When introducing Room (see the playlists persistence issue), model this properly instead of porting the sentinel: - playlists table gets a kind column: NORMAL / FAVORITES , with a constraint/guarantee that exactly one FAVORITES row exists. - Migration path: a legacy row named "favoritos" becomes kind = FAVORITES , not a name match. - Export keeps writing name: "favoritos", id: 1 in the backup JSON, so backups produced by the new app remain readable by the old app (forward compat for free). Scope - Part of the Room playlists work: decide kind vs alternatives in…
descriptions.github:5670078564: Spike to investigate a better implementation of history state for agents/MCP. Based on conversation in 68 On "not ideal": one alternative keeps the change undoable in Edit mode. Undo.undo() and redo() apply a selection entry when entry.selection before instanceof UndoSystem.selectionSave , and they only call its load() . A subclass that snapshots the texture's own selection (by UUID) and restores it in load() doesn't depend on UVEditor.texture : I tried it live with risky eval , in Edit mode with nothing in the UV editor. Undo cleared the 16 selected pixels and kept the texture, and Redo brought them back. The trade-off: it relies on UndoSystem.selectionSave and on pushing to Undo.history directly, with the same bookkeeping as finishSelection (trim the redo branch, undo limit , index ). It should also record nothing when Undo Selection is off or in an Edit Session, like the native path…

descriptions.github:5669968637: The report persists theme in localStorage ( revai.config ), but filters reset on every reload. Do - Extend revai.config persistence to: search text, severity filter, file filter, group collapse state. - Restore them on load, next to the existing theme restore. - Add a "Reset filters" affordance (or reuse the existing clear buttons) so stale filters can be dropped for good. Files - skills/revai/templates/review.html only. AC - Apply filters → reload → filters still applied. - Clearing filters persists too (no phantom filters on next open). Suggested commit: feat(report): persist filter state ( 8) — see CONTRIBUTING.md for scopes.

descriptions.github:5669910043: The gap docs/architecture/overview.md lists this under Known gaps , added in 2140: The retry wait() in workspace-changes.ts never removes its abort listener when its timer fires, so a stream that keeps dropping, as it does while the API is down, adds one listener to the workspace's signal per attempt, about 360 an hour, until the last list leaves. It also waits out its timer when the signal is already aborted, so a stream torn down between attempts takes up to 10 seconds to stop. Why it matters The sources panel and the Studio list share this one stream per workspace since 2126, and it reconnects whenever it drops: the API restarts, the machine sleeps, the sidecar crashes. While the API stays down, follow() retries every 10 seconds, and each retry's wait() leaves a closure on the signal, holding its timer and its settled promise, until the workspace is left. Nothing breaks and nothing…

descriptions.github:5669640859: Goal Add a small check for broken or malformed external references in maintained skill and README documentation. Acceptance criteria - Restrict checks to relevant checked-in Markdown files and HTTP(S) references. - Report the file and URL for failures; handle redirects and fragments without treating a valid page as broken. - Keep the default validator usable with the Python standard library; document any optional network check separately. - Provide a deterministic offline test or fixture for URL extraction and reporting behavior. - Do not make CI network checks flaky or fail silently on transient network errors. Avoid automatically rewriting links; report actionable results for a contributor to review.
descriptions.github:5669640596: Goal Add a concise, tool-neutral scorecard template that helps teams define a RAG evaluation before comparing pipeline changes. Acceptance criteria - Include dataset version, query, expected answer or claims, expected sources, answerability, and access-control context. - Include retrieval, grounding/citation, answer quality, latency, and cost measures where applicable. - Explain that metric definitions and thresholds must be selected for the use case; do not imply one aggregate score proves production readiness. - Provide brief scoring instructions and an example row using synthetic content. - Link to primary metric documentation where the template names a specific metric. Do not add a vendor dependency or sensitive example data.
descriptions.github:5669640738: Goal Add a short troubleshooting section for when a skill is installed but an agent does not discover or invoke it. Acceptance criteria - Cover the documented paths for OpenCode, Codex, and Claude Code. - Include checks for the SKILL.md frontmatter, folder/skill name, project versus global placement, active working directory, and restarting or refreshing the session where appropriate. - Link discovery behavior to each client's current official documentation. - Clearly label client-specific details and avoid assuming undocumented behavior is universal. descriptions.github:5669579562: What happened? The COMPOSABLE scoring tent currently penalizes modules with extreme stability ($I = 0.00$), dropping their score to 0%. While this penalty makes sense for high-level orchestration modules, it creates a false positive penalty for leaf utility files (e.g., basic UI components, data structures, or primitive helpers) that are intended to have zero efferent coupling ($C e = 0$). Example Scenario 1. A foundational UI file ( menu.rs ) has low initial coupling ($C a + C e < 2$), causing Topos to fall back to a neutral $I = 0.50$ midpoint score (quality = 1.0, overall score 80%). 2. Additional features adopt menu.rs , raising afferent coupling ($C a \ge 2$). 3. Because menu.rs relies on no other internal modules ($C e = 0$), its instability now resolves to $I = 0.00$. 4. Result: Topos penalizes the file for extreme stability, dropping its score from 80% to 0.0% and triggering a…

descriptions.github:5669313294: Status: READY TO IMPLEMENT What is wrong On Windows, a camera republish after a LiveKit reconnect re-applies the startup allocation floor but never schedules its release, so the floor stays on the wire for the rest of the call. RoomConnection::republish camera after reconnect ( apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/transport/publisher.rs ) republishes with camera publish options(width, height, self.published frame rate) , which resolves the floor through startup allocation floor . descriptions.github:5668929040: Description Under pushback, models often abandon a correct answer even when the user brings no new evidence. SYCON-Bench (arXiv ) measures this as turn of first flip and number of flips. This differs from coherence across turns : a flip is consistent with what the user just said, so a coherence judge doesn't penalize it. Proposed Change 1. Add stance stability with cot reasons to LLMProvider . The judge: - identifies each claim or answer the assistant committed to; - finds later turns where the user disputed it; - decides whether the assistant changed position, and whether the user's turn gave new evidence or arguments. 2. Score = 1.0 if every change of position followed new evidence. It drops with each unsupported change. 3. meta holds the first unsupported flip turn and the number of flips. Usage Example Files to Reference - src/feedback/trulens/feedback/templates/conversation.py…
descriptions.github:5668928345: Description Assistants sometimes repeat themselves across turns: the same reply, the same fallback phrase ("I'm sorry, I can't help with that"), or growing boilerplate. Opik's ConversationDegenerationMetric checks for this without an LLM. TruLens has no deterministic conversation metric. This is a metric, not a record stat, because it needs reply content and conversation grouping. Both are available at evaluation time but not in the per-record stats. Proposed Change 1. Add a deterministic metric conversation repetition . For each assistant turn it computes: - n-gram repetition within the reply; - overlap with the previous assistant reply ; - known fallback phrases , from a configurable list; - lexical diversity. 2. The four signals are averaged into a per-turn score. The conversation score = 1 − the worst turn's score. meta holds the per-turn breakdown. 3. No LLM calls. Usage Example…
descriptions.github:5668927603: Description The existing conversation judges all score the assistant's turns. The user's turns often say more about whether the conversation went well: repeated requests, corrections ("no, I meant..."), "that's wrong", giving up. Opik ships UserFrustrationMetric . openevals ships USER SATISFACTION PROMPT and PERCEIVED ERROR PROMPT . SPUR (arXiv ) learns satisfaction rubrics from user utterances. Proposed Change 1. Add user frustration with cot reasons to LLMProvider . The judge reads the user turns, with the assistant turns as context. It identifies: - repeated requests - corrections of the assistant - explicit statements of error or dissatisfaction - abandonment 2. Score = 1.0 for no signs of frustration, down to 0.0 for a user who gave up or repeatedly corrected the assistant. meta lists each signal with its turn. Usage Example Files to Reference…
descriptions.github:5668926852: Description Users set constraints early in a conversation ("answer in JSON", "only cover the EU", "never suggest X"). Models drift from them in later turns. Multi-IF (arXiv ) finds instruction-following accuracy drops across turns, and defines: - Instruction forgetting ratio: instructions followed in one turn but not the next, as a share of those followed. - Error correction ratio: instructions missed earlier but followed later. MultiChallenge (arXiv ) treats instruction retention as one of four core multi-turn challenges. The existing conversation judges don't look at instructions across turns. Proposed Change 1. Add instruction retention with cot reasons to LLMProvider . The judge: - extracts the standing instructions from user turns, noting the turn each was given and whether a later turn revoked it; - checks each later assistant turn against the instructions in force at that point…

So a conversation judge can't tell an answer grounded in a successful tool call from a guess after the tool failed. It also can't see a coding session's edits and test runs across turns. Proposed Change 1. Add include tool calls: bool = False to Selector.select conversation() ( src/core/trulens/core/feedback/selector.py:770 ). It's off by default because it changes what existing judges see and can add many tokens. 2. When on, each turn also gets its TOOL and MCP spans, ordered by start time, as "tool calls": [{"name", "arguments", "result", "error"}] . These come from gen…
descriptions.github:5668925550: Description Repositories give coding agents rules in AGENTS.md , CLAUDE.md or .cursorrules : which commands to run, which paths not to touch, how to format and test. GPA's Plan Adherence checks the agent's own plan, and Tool Selection checks mandated tools only. Neither takes the repository's rules as input. Braintrust's write-up on behavior scoring for coding agents (braintrust.dev/evals/behavior-vs-output-scoring) scores rule compliance with a deterministic check and an LLM judge, against an open format (github.com/braintrustdata/agentbehavior). It found that calls blocked before they ran must not count as violations: in its run, a naive check got 7 of 9 flags wrong. Proposed Change 1. Add project rule adherence with cot reasons to LLMProvider . Inputs: the rules text and the trace. 2. The judge gives each checkable rule a verdict: followed, violated (citing span ids) or not…
descriptions.github:5668924864: Description The GPA judges score how an agent worked, not whether it did what was asked. agent goal accuracy gives one pass/fail over a conversation transcript. A request usually has several requirements, and agents often meet some of them. Agent-as-a-Judge (arXiv ) scores requirements one at a time, and also counts a requirement as met only when the requirements it depends on are met. DeepEval TaskCompletion and Opik AgentTaskCompletionJudge are single-score versions. Proposed Change 1. Add requirement satisfaction with cot reasons to LLMProvider . Inputs: the request, the output, and an optional explicit requirement list. 2. Without a list, the judge extracts requirements from the request first, then judges each against the output as met, partly met or not met, with evidence. 3. Score = (met + 0.5 × partly met) ÷ total. Per-requirement verdicts go in meta . 4. Accept any of three…
descriptions.github:5668924148: Description Coding agents run shell commands with the user's permissions. OpenAgentSafety (arXiv ) and AgentTrust (arXiv ) catalogue the risky ones: - deleting outside the workspace; - reading or printing credentials; - piping a downloaded script into a shell; - rewriting shared history; - editing agent settings to skip confirmations. AgentTrust pairs near-identical safe and unsafe commands ( rm -rf ./node modules versus rm -rf / ), so keyword matching alone over-flags. GPA has no safety dimension, and Braintrust, LangSmith and Opik don't ship a metric for this. Proposed Change 1. Add a rule-based prefilter over the turn's shell commands and edited paths. It reports each match with a category: - delete outside workspace - credential read - remote script exec - history rewrite - agent permission change Commands are judged relative to CODING AGENT.WORKSPACE when path capture is on. 2. EvilGenie (arXiv ) uses test-file edit detection as one of its reward-hacking checks. ImpossibleBench (arXiv ) measures how often agents pass tasks that can't be solved honestly. Users can override the globs with test file globs . 3. The judge reads those diffs, plus the turn's source diffs, and…
descriptions.github:5668922741: Description Agents sometimes call tools with arguments that don't match the tool's schema: missing required fields, wrong types, unknown keys. GPA's Tool Calling judge catches this among other things, but it's an LLM call per trace. This check is deterministic and can run on every tool call. Two things are missing: - A way to select just the tool calls. Today the choice is a single span attribute or the whole trace ( Selector(trace level=True) ). The whole trace passes every LLM turn, retrieval and payload to a metric that only needs tool names and arguments. That's wasted serialization for deterministic metrics and wasted tokens for judges. The pieces already exist on Selector ( src/core/trulens/core/feedback/selector.py ): span type , span attributes processor , and collect list=True (which gathers every match in a record into one list). But there's no factory for it, and span type…

descriptions.github:5668920124: Description Providers report how many input tokens came from their prompt cache. TruLens doesn't record it. The OpenAI endpoint reads only prompt tokens , completion tokens and total tokens ( src/providers/openai/trulens/providers/openai/endpoint.py:564-566 ). descriptions.github:5668919451: Description Client hooks trace Claude Code, Cursor and OpenCode sessions. With the default capture flags off, nothing recorded shows whether the agent tested its change: - Exit codes. The parser doesn't list exit code in known keys ( src/core/trulens/core/otel/client hooks/parsers.py:180 ), so it lands in metadata . The privacy filter then drops it, because only SAFE METADATA KEYS survive ( privacy.py:17 ). - Commands. These are recorded only as tool input , and only with TRULENS CAPTURE TOOL PAYLOADS . Without the text, a test run can't be told apart from any other command. - Edited file paths. These are recorded only with TRULENS CAPTURE PATHS , so an edit to a test file can't be told apart from any other edit. Finishing without checking the change is a common coding-agent failure. "The Danger of Overthinking" (Cuadron et al., arXiv ) calls it premature disengagement and links it to…
descriptions.github:5668905028: Right now in a training run, all the dimer configurations in a node are sent to compute the energy by the force routines one by one. If we have 1000 dimer conformations for water-water, the force routines are called 1000 times. This prevents optimisation, let alone porting to GPUs. The first step to optimise this would be that the force routines should be called once and handle 1000 dimers. This would allow using SIMD on CPUs and gives us 3-8 times the performance we have now for training. To be able to do this, the deviation from the reference has to be computed at once. The next step would be to run all the dimers on a node in a single force call rather than one per dimer. If that is possible it may be feasible to port to GPUs.
